why-crm-data-goes-stale.title: Why CRM data goes stale — and what actually fixes it
why-crm-data-goes-stale.excerpt: Most CRM data isn't wrong because reps are careless. It's wrong because logging it is extra work with no immediate payoff.

body.text: Ask any sales leader what they'd fix first about their CRM and "data quality" comes up almost every time. But the usual response — more mandatory fields, stricter validation, quarterly "CRM hygiene" pushes — treats the symptom, not the cause.
The real problem: logging is a tax on selling

Every manual CRM update is time a rep isn't spending with a prospect. When updating a deal stage requires opening a separate tab, finding the record, and typing a summary, reps do it inconsistently — not because they don't care, but because the system asks them to context-switch away from the thing they're paid to do.
The fix isn't more process. It's removing the manual step entirely.
What actually works

items: Automated activity logging from email and calendar, so the record updates itself
AI-drafted call summaries attached to the deal automatically
Deal stage suggestions based on real signals, not a dropdown a rep forgets to change

body.text: Teams that make this shift don't just get cleaner data — they get pipeline visibility that reflects what's actually happening, not what got typed in during a Friday afternoon cleanup.

ai-crm-vs-spreadsheets.title: AI CRM vs. spreadsheets: what changes when you switch
ai-crm-vs-spreadsheets.excerpt: Spreadsheets are flexible until they aren't. Here's what actually breaks first as a sales team scales past them.

body.text: Spreadsheets are a genuinely good tool for a two-person sales team. The trouble starts around the fifth or sixth rep, when two people are editing the same tab, formulas break silently, and "who owns this lead" becomes a Slack thread instead of a field.
Where it breaks first

Ownership conflicts and version drift are usually the first cracks. The second is reporting: a spreadsheet can show you today's pipeline, but reconstructing last month's isn't something most teams bother doing, which makes forecast accuracy nearly impossible to improve.
We didn't switch because the spreadsheet broke. We switched because nobody trusted the numbers in it anymore.

That's the real trigger for most teams — not a technical failure, but a trust failure. Once forecast numbers stop matching reality, the spreadsheet stops being useful even if it still technically works.

lead-response-time-benchmark.title: What's a good lead response time in 2026?
lead-response-time-benchmark.excerpt: "Respond fast" is common advice. Here's what the actual numbers look like, and why the first five minutes matter more than the next five hours.

body.text: Lead response time gets cited constantly, but the benchmark itself is often misquoted. The consistent finding across response-time research: conversion likelihood drops sharply after the first five minutes, then drops again after the first hour.
Why five minutes, specifically

It's not magic — it's attention. A visitor who just filled out a form is still on your site, still thinking about the problem they came to solve. An hour later, they've moved on to three other tabs and two other vendors.
What actually slows teams down

items: Manual lead qualification before routing
Leads sitting in a shared inbox instead of being assigned automatically
No clear ownership rule for territory or company size

body.text: None of these are people problems — they're routing problems. Automating qualification and assignment is usually the single highest-leverage fix.

smb-tooling-checklist.title: The 5-tool checklist every growing SMB outgrows
smb-tooling-checklist.excerpt: Spreadsheet CRM, separate email tool, separate forms, separate analytics, separate automation — here's when each one starts costing more than it saves.

body.text: Most SMBs don't set out to run five disconnected tools. It happens gradually: a spreadsheet for leads, an email tool for campaigns, a forms plugin for the website, a separate analytics dashboard, and eventually a Zapier chain trying to hold it all together.
The tell that it's time to consolidate

The clearest signal isn't cost — it's the moment someone asks "how many leads did we get from last week's campaign" and the honest answer requires checking three different tools and reconciling them by hand.
At that point, the integration tax (time spent connecting and reconciling tools) usually exceeds what a unified platform would cost outright.

marketing-attribution-explained.title: Marketing attribution, explained without the jargon
marketing-attribution-explained.excerpt: First-touch, last-touch, multi-touch — the terminology is confusing, but the underlying question is simple: what actually drove this deal?

body.text: Attribution models exist to answer one question: when a deal closes, which marketing touches deserve credit? The honest answer is usually "several of them," which is why single-touch models (first-touch, last-touch) tend to mislead more than they help.
Why multi-touch models tend to win

A prospect might read a blog post, ignore three emails, attend a webinar, and finally convert after a demo. Crediting only the demo (last-touch) makes top-of-funnel content look worthless — even though it's what got the prospect there in the first place.

The practical requirement for multi-touch attribution isn't a fancier model — it's a single data model where marketing touches and CRM deal data actually live together, instead of being reconciled after the fact.

ai-assistants-explained.title: What "AI Assistants embedded in your CRM" actually means
ai-assistants-explained.excerpt: Not a chatbot bolted onto the sidebar. Here's what it looks like when AI is grounded in your actual pipeline data.

body.text: "AI-powered" has become a label nearly every SaaS product claims, which makes it worth being specific about what it actually means in a CRM context.
Grounded vs. generic

A generic AI assistant answers questions using general knowledge. A grounded assistant answers using your actual deal history, your actual email threads, and your actual pipeline data — which is the difference between a plausible-sounding follow-up email and one that references the right proposal, the right objection, and the right next step.
Where it fits in the workflow

items: Drafting follow-up emails from real call and email context
Summarizing calls automatically into the CRM record
Flagging deals with declining engagement before they go cold

body.text: The common thread: the AI works inside the tools reps already use, on data that's already there — not as a separate destination they have to remember to check.

no-code-workflow-patterns.title: Five no-code workflow patterns worth stealing
no-code-workflow-patterns.excerpt: Practical automation patterns that connect CRM, marketing, and support without a single engineering ticket.

body.text: The best workflow automations aren't clever — they're the boring hand-offs that used to require someone remembering to do them manually.

items: Auto-create an onboarding task list the moment a deal closes
Route a support ticket to sales when a churn-risk keyword appears
Trigger a re-engagement campaign after 30 days of no activity
Escalate a deal for approval when a discount exceeds a threshold
Notify a CSM automatically when usage drops below a baseline

body.text: None of these require custom code — they require a trigger, a condition, and an action, chained together once and left to run.

getting-started.title: Getting started with ZynReach
getting-started.description: Set up your workspace and connect your first tool.

body.text: This guide walks through the first steps after signing up: creating your workspace, inviting teammates, and connecting your first integration.
1. Create your workspace
After signup, you'll be prompted to name your workspace and choose your primary use case (Sales, Marketing, or both). This determines which capabilities are surfaced first in your navigation.
2. Invite your team
From Settings → Team, invite teammates by email. Each invited user is prompted to set a password and complete their profile on first login.
3. Connect your first tool
Go to Settings → Integrations to connect email, calendar, or another supported tool. Most integrations complete in under two minutes via OAuth.

connecting-email.title: Connecting your email and calendar
connecting-email.description: Sync email and calendar activity so the CRM logs itself.

body.text: Connecting email and calendar is what powers ZynReach's automated activity logging — without it, CRM records won't update themselves.
Supported providers

items: Google Workspace
Microsoft 365 / Outlook
Any IMAP-compatible provider

body.text: Connect via Settings → Integrations → Email & Calendar. You'll be redirected to your provider's OAuth consent screen — ZynReach never asks for your email password directly.

crm-pipeline-setup.title: Setting up your sales pipeline
crm-pipeline-setup.description: Customize deal stages to match how your team actually sells.

body.text: Every workspace starts with a default pipeline (New → Qualified → Proposal → Closed Won/Lost), but most teams customize stages to match their actual sales process.
Editing pipeline stages

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
body: Zyntra Digital, as the operator of the ZynReach platform, is committed to protecting the privacy of users and the personal data processed through the ZynReach website, services, and digital platform. Data protection and privacy are a core part of how ZynReach is designed and operated, and the company applies appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect data from unauthorized access, use, alteration, disclosure, or loss.

ZynReach approaches privacy according to the principles of transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, security, and accountability. This policy explains what data we may collect and its sources, how we use it, the legal bases for processing, when it is shared, the rights of data subjects, and how data is protected, retained, deleted, and transferred internationally.

sections.heading: 2. The Entity Responsible for Processing
body: For the purposes of this policy, "ZynReach," "Zyntra Digital," "the Company," "we," and "us" refer to the entity operating ZynReach's services, which operates from Egypt.

Contact details: privacy@zynreach.com for privacy matters, legal@zynreach.com for legal matters, info@zynreach.com for general inquiries. Address: 63 C Al Ashgar Street, Al Haram, Giza Governorate 12556, Egypt.

sections.heading: 3. Scope of This Policy
body: This policy applies to data processed through the ZynReach website, user accounts, the ZynReach SaaS platform, and on-site forms, including in particular:
list: Free trial, demo, and sales requests; customer service and support; and marketing communications.
Integrations and APIs; analytics and business-data services; and CRM and marketing tools.
AI features, documents uploaded by users, billing and subscription operations, and security and compliance operations.
This policy does not apply to third-party services or websites not controlled by ZynReach.

sections.heading: 4. Account & Organization Data
body: When creating an account, we may collect name, company name, email address, phone number, job title, country, login data, account preferences, language and time-zone settings, and data of users associated with the organization.

When using Enterprise services or organization management, information such as the organization's name, structure, branches, departments, roles, permissions, security settings, and custom domains may be processed — ZynReach already provides capabilities for organizational identity, branches, custom domains, and other organization settings.

sections.heading: 5. Data Entered by the User & Customer Responsibility
body: The user or customer may enter data within the platform, such as customer data, leads, employee data, supplier data, contacts, notes, documents, invoices, transaction records, project data, and support, marketing, and communication data — this data may include personal information relating to other individuals.

When the customer enters personal data belonging to its employees, customers, or suppliers, the customer is responsible for ensuring it has the necessary lawful basis to process that data, has provided the required notices to the data subjects, has not entered data it lacks the right to process, complies with the laws applicable to its own activities, and uses ZynReach in a manner consistent with the agreement and the Data Processing Agreement.

sections.heading: 6. ZynReach as Processor and as Controller
body: When ZynReach processes personal data on the customer's behalf and per its instructions, it acts as a Processor, and the customer is the Controller that determines the purposes and means of processing; in this case processing is governed by the commercial agreement and the applicable Data Processing Agreement (DPA), which provides that the company processes personal data based on the customer's documented instructions, except as required by law.

In other cases — such as website administration, marketing, lead management, user accounts, sales, support, security, analytics, and business relationships — ZynReach may act as a Controller that determines the purposes and means of processing under applicable law.

sections.heading: 7. Automatically Collected Data, Usage Data & Audit Logs
body: When visiting the website or using the platform, technical information may be collected, such as IP address, device type, operating system, browser type, device or session identifiers, pages visited, time and duration of the visit, referral source, performance information, and error logs — used for security, running the service, performance improvement, analytics, and detecting abuse.

ZynReach may also record information about how the services are used (features used, operations performed, login times, searches, errors), linked to the user's or organization's account where necessary. Audit logs help organizations track activity within the platform (user identity, the operation performed, its time, the affected resource, and the changes made) in a searchable record, consistent with security, governance, and legal requirements.

sections.heading: 8. Business Data & Lead Generation
body: ZynReach provides capabilities related to company and contact discovery, building lead lists, and data enrichment; certain company or contact data may accordingly be processed from public sources, commercial sources, data providers, or licensed databases, and may include name, job title, company name, professional email, professional phone number, company information, industry, location, and firmographic and technographic data.

Information being publicly available does not mean it is "non-personal," nor that its use is not subject to applicable law; ZynReach handles personal data according to its nature and the applicable law, not merely its source. Data obtained from external providers may be subject to that source's own usage terms or licensing restrictions.

sections.heading: 9. Purposes of Processing
body: ZynReach may use personal data for the following purposes:
list: Providing the service: account creation, running the platform, authentication, executing operations, delivering features, and organization administration.
Customer support and sales: responding to inquiries, processing support requests, following up on demo requests, and managing leads and the commercial relationship.
Marketing: sending marketing communications, delivering relevant content, and measuring campaign effectiveness — subject to any consent or opt-out requirements imposed by law.
Security and compliance: detecting attacks, preventing fraud, protecting accounts, investigating incidents, fulfilling legal obligations, and responding to legitimate government requests.
Analytics: understanding service usage, improving products and user experience, and measuring performance.

sections.heading: 10. Legal Basis for Processing
body: Depending on the nature of the processing and applicable law, ZynReach may rely on contract performance or pre-contractual steps, legitimate interest, consent, legal obligation, or the protection of vital interests where applicable — ZynReach does not rely on a single legal basis for all types of processing.

Where ZynReach relies on legitimate interest (such as platform security, fraud prevention, service improvement, or managing business relationships), it ensures the processing is necessary for the stated purpose, does not exceed what is required, and does not unjustifiably override the individual's rights and interests. Where consent is legally required, ZynReach seeks to obtain it clearly, and the user may withdraw it at any time.

sections.heading: 11. Marketing Communications
body: ZynReach may send operational messages, account notifications, security messages, service updates, and support messages, alongside marketing offers and educational content; the ability to opt out of each type varies by its nature, and messages necessary for account operation or security cannot be opted out of.

Users can unsubscribe from marketing communications via the unsubscribe link, account settings, or by contacting ZynReach, while ZynReach remains able to send messages necessary for the service, security, or contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 12. Cookies
body: ZynReach may use cookies and similar technologies, including:
list: Essential cookies necessary to run the website or platform, and security cookies that help protect sessions and accounts.
Analytics cookies used to understand how the site is used, and preference cookies used to remember user settings.
Marketing cookies that may be used to measure campaigns where legally permitted.
Where required by law, a tool is presented allowing the user to manage their preferences; disabling certain cookies may affect some site or service functionality.

sections.heading: 13. Data Sharing & Sub-processors
body: ZynReach does not sell personal data merely to generate revenue from its sale. Data may be shared, when necessary, with infrastructure, email, analytics, customer-support, payment, and security providers, sub-processors, professional advisors, and government authorities where disclosure is legally required — the current Compliance page sets out the categories of these providers and their processing locations.

When ZynReach processes data on the customer's behalf, it may use sub-processors to deliver parts of the service; this relationship is governed by the Data Processing Agreement and applicable legal and contractual requirements.

sections.heading: 14. Legal Disclosure & Business Transfers
body: ZynReach may disclose data where required by law, court order, or a competent government authority, or where necessary to protect legal rights, investigate fraud, or protect the safety of users — disclosures are limited, as far as possible, to what is necessary for the lawful purpose.

In the event of a merger, acquisition, restructuring, or sale of part of the business, some data may be transferred as part of the transaction, subject to applicable laws and data-protection obligations, and data subjects will be notified where required by law.

sections.heading: 15. Data Protection & Shared Security Responsibility
body: ZynReach applies technical and organizational measures that include, depending on the service and environment, encryption in transit and at rest, least privilege, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, audit logging, system monitoring, backups, vulnerability management, and incident response — consistent with what the current Security page describes. Even so, no system or network can be guaranteed absolute protection from all risks.

Protecting data is not ZynReach's responsibility alone; the customer and user bear responsibilities including protecting their login credentials, using strong passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication, not sharing accounts, managing users, reviewing permissions, securing devices, and not sending unnecessary data.

sections.heading: 16. Data Retention & Deletion
body: ZynReach retains data only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purpose it was collected for, or for the period required by law, contract, accounting requirements, security requirements, or dispute-resolution and fraud-prevention requirements; retention periods vary by data type and purpose.

Once data is no longer needed, ZynReach seeks to delete it or render it unidentifiable in accordance with its applicable procedures and policies; some data may persist for a limited time in backups and security and audit logs. Deleting data from the user interface does not necessarily mean it is immediately removed from every backup copy.

sections.heading: 17. Children's Data & Sensitive Data
body: ZynReach's services are not directed at children, and ZynReach does not intend to collect personal data from children without the required lawful basis or consent; if ZynReach learns it has unlawfully collected a child's data, it may take appropriate steps to delete it.

Users should not upload sensitive personal data (such as health, biometric, sensitive financial, or data concerning origin, religion, beliefs, or sex life) to ZynReach unless necessary for the service, the customer has an appropriate lawful basis, and appropriate safeguards have been applied.

sections.heading: 18. Artificial Intelligence & Data
body: ZynReach offers features such as AI Assistants, AI Agents, and AI Insights within the platform; these features may use data available within the scope of the service to perform the function the user requests, applying controls intended to restrict access, respect permissions, log activity, and minimize unnecessary data — certain AI Agent capabilities include human-approval checkpoints and an activity audit log.

Users should not input personal or confidential data into AI tools unless they have the right to do so and the feature is designed to process such data. AI outputs within ZynReach should not be interpreted as final legal, medical, financial, or employment decisions merely because they were produced by an automated system; where a decision has a material effect on an individual, the organization using ZynReach must ensure appropriate human oversight and legal basis are in place.

sections.heading: 19. Data Subject Rights
body: Depending on applicable law, an individual may have the following rights regarding their personal data:
list: The right of access: to request to know what data is being processed and obtain a copy of it, where permitted by law.
The right to rectification: to request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.
The right to erasure: to request deletion of data where permitted by law.
The right to restrict processing, and the right to object to certain types of processing.
The right to withdraw consent where processing relies on it, and the right to data portability where applicable.
Additional rights relating to automated decision-making, where applicable law provides for them.

sections.heading: 20. How to Exercise Your Rights
body: Privacy requests can be submitted via privacy@zynreach.com; ZynReach may request additional information to verify the requester's identity before fulfilling the request, particularly where disclosure could reveal another person's personal data, and only to the extent reasonably necessary for verification.

If the customer submits a request relating to other individuals' data stored within its account, ZynReach may be required to refer it to the customer as the party controlling that data, in accordance with the Data Processing Agreement, the customer's instructions, and applicable law.

sections.heading: 21. Regulatory Requests & International Transfers
body: When ZynReach receives a lawful request for data, it reviews it as permitted by law and determines the scope of the information requested, and may decline or object to it if it is unlawful, unclear, or exceeds the requesting authority's powers, unless prohibited by law from doing so.

Data may be processed in a country other than the one where the user resides; customer data is hosted by default in data centers within the United States, with regional options available for Enterprise plans by agreement. Where legal restrictions apply to international transfers, ZynReach seeks to apply an appropriate lawful transfer mechanism and safeguards, as detailed in the Data Processing Agreement.

sections.heading: 22. Service Providers, Payment Data & Support
body: When a third party is used to process personal data, ZynReach seeks to apply appropriate measures including contractual review, data-protection requirements, access restrictions, and confidentiality obligations. When purchasing paid services, payment data is processed through specialized payment providers, and users should not send full payment card details via email.
When contacting the ZynReach team, support correspondence, issue details, and attached files may be retained for the purposes of providing support, resolving issues, quality assurance, and security.

sections.heading: 23. Analytics & Third-Party Links
body: ZynReach may use analytics tools to understand website performance, platform usage, user journeys, errors, and conversions; some of this data may be processed by third-party analytics providers listed among the sub-processor categories on the Compliance page.

The ZynReach website may contain links to third-party websites or services whose privacy policies and data practices ZynReach does not control; users should review a third party's own privacy policy before providing it with personal information.

sections.heading: 24. Security Incidents & Data Breaches
body: If ZynReach discovers a security incident affecting personal data, it assesses the nature of the incident, the type of data, the number of individuals affected, the level of risk, and legal and contractual requirements; the customer, data subjects, or regulators may be notified where legally or contractually required. Not every alert, failed login attempt, vulnerability, or technical error automatically constitutes a personal data breach — this is determined based on the facts, the risk involved, and applicable law.
ZynReach may retain records relating to consents, data subject requests, incidents, disclosures, and audits for as long as necessary for compliance, governance, and the defense of legal rights.

sections.heading: 25. Changes to This Policy
body: ZynReach may update this policy from time to time due to product development, new services, technical or legal changes, changes in vendors, or changes in data-processing practices; the updated version is published on the website with the last-updated date noted. Where a change is material and significantly affects users' rights, ZynReach may take additional steps to notify users as required by applicable law.

sections.heading: 26. Relationship to Other Documents
body: This policy, by itself, does not create contractual obligations beyond those set out in the Terms of Service, the master agreement, the Data Processing Agreement, an Enterprise Agreement, or a Service Level Agreement; in case of conflict, the applicable legal agreement and applicable law govern. This policy also grants no user any right to ZynReach's source code, algorithms, trade secrets, security architecture, or internal documentation.

This Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected, used, shared, and protected, while the Security & Trust Policy explains the security, technical, and organizational framework ZynReach uses to protect the platform and its data; neither document replaces the other. Publishing this policy does not, by itself, grant anyone an automatic right to restricted security documentation, which is governed by the separate Security & Compliance Documentation Request Policy.

sections.heading: 27. Regulatory Compliance (GDPR & CCPA)
body: ZynReach seeks to develop its privacy and security practices in line with relevant regulatory frameworks, and currently addresses GDPR in relation to lawful basis, data subject rights, and the Data Processing Agreement, and CCPA in relation to California residents' rights, alongside SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-aligned practices within the disclosed scope of controls — without this meaning that using ZynReach automatically makes the customer compliant with every requirement of any given law or standard.

ZynReach does not sell personal data merely to sell it to third parties, and any legal term such as "sale" or "sharing" is interpreted according to the definition set out in applicable law. Where ZynReach becomes legally obligated to provide a separate "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" mechanism, it will provide the appropriate mechanism for users covered by that law. A data subject has the right, where permitted by law, to lodge a complaint with the competent data-protection authority in the country or region in which they reside.

sections.heading: 28. Legal Disclaimer
body: This policy has been prepared to transparently and clearly explain ZynReach's privacy and data-protection practices, and does not constitute legal advice, a guarantee that the customer complies with applicable laws, an amendment to any existing commercial agreement, or a substitute for the Data Processing Agreement or the Terms of Service. Every organization should assess the nature of its own data, the location of its customers, applicable regulatory requirements, and obtain independent legal advice where necessary.

sections.heading: 29. Contact Us
body: For all privacy requests: Privacy Team — privacy@zynreach.com (a request should ideally include name, email address, company if applicable, the nature of the request, and a description of the data requested).

For legal inquiries and Data Processing Agreement requests: legal@zynreach.com. To report a security issue: security@zynreach.com (passwords, API keys, or sensitive customer data should never be sent via email).

sections.heading: 1. Purpose of the Policy
body: This policy explains the principles and rules ZynReach (owned and operated by Zyntra Digital) follows regarding the retention, deletion, and secure destruction of data, so that data is kept only for as long as necessary to fulfill the lawful purpose it was collected for, and personal data is not retained longer than necessary, subject to legal and contractual requirements.

The policy also aims to protect data throughout its retention period, preserve ZynReach's ability to maintain business continuity and disaster recovery, and strike an appropriate balance between privacy, security, and operational and legal requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of Application
body: This policy applies to data ZynReach collects, stores, processes, or manages within its website and platform, customer and user accounts, databases, support and communication systems, system and security logs, backups, monitoring and analytics systems, and account and billing management systems, as well as third-party services that process data on ZynReach's behalf, as applicable — it does not necessarily apply to every type of data with the same duration or deletion mechanism.

sections.heading: 3. Core Principles of Data Retention
body: ZynReach adheres to the following principles:
list: Purpose limitation: data is not retained merely because it might be useful in the future, absent a specific lawful purpose.
Data minimization: retaining only the minimum necessary to fulfill the lawful purpose of processing.

Defining the retention period according to the nature of the data, its purpose, and legal, contractual, and operational requirements, while it remains subject to appropriate security controls throughout that period.

Secure deletion once the retention period ends or the lawful need lapses, while acknowledging that ZynReach may be obligated to retain certain data longer due to law, disputes, or accounting or contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 4. Categories of Data
body: For retention-management purposes, data is classified into categories including:
list: Account data (name, email, login data, organization data and settings), and Customer Data entered or uploaded through the platform.
Usage data (login records, usage and performance information, technical events), and security logs (authentication, access, and audit events).
Support data (requests, correspondence, attachments), and billing data (subscriptions, invoices, payment records).
Website data (contact forms, trial requests, newsletter sign-ups, per the Privacy Policy).

sections.heading: 5. Data Retention Schedule
body: ZynReach uses a general retention framework based on the purpose of processing, the nature of the data, and legal obligations:
list: Customer account data: for the duration of the account and contractual relationship. Customer Data: for the duration of the service, per the DPA and agreement.
User data: for the duration the account is active, then per related obligations. Support data: for as long as necessary for support purposes and legal obligations.
Security and audit logs: per security, operational, and legal requirements. Billing data: per applicable accounting and legal requirements.
Marketing data: until consent is withdrawn or the purpose ends. Backups: per the applicable backup retention cycle.
This schedule should not be read as imposing a fixed duration for all data in every case; the period may vary where the nature of the data, the law, the contract, or security risk requires.

sections.heading: 6. Customer Data & Retention Responsibility
body: When ZynReach processes Customer Data on the Customer's behalf as a Processor, the Customer remains responsible for determining the appropriate retention period as the Controller, unless the agreement or law provides otherwise. Under the Data Processing Agreement, ZynReach processes data per the Customer's instructions, retains it for as long as necessary to provide the services, applies deletion or return procedures when the relationship ends, and manages backups per applicable operational controls.

sections.heading: 7. End of Customer Subscription & Data Deletion
body: The end of a Customer's subscription does not necessarily mean all its data is deleted immediately; ZynReach may need a transition period to close the account, disable access, process export or retrieval requests, carry out deletion, handle backups, and meet legal obligations. The procedures and timeframes specified in the DPA or the commercial agreement remain the primary reference for Customer Data.

Where deletion is required, ZynReach seeks to delete the data from relevant operational systems using appropriate procedures (removing database records, deleting stored files, revoking access permissions, destroying associated encryption keys where applicable), while acknowledging that immediate deletion from all backups may not be possible given how backup systems operate.

sections.heading: 8. Backups
body: ZynReach uses backups for business continuity, disaster recovery, service restoration, and protection against data loss; some deleted data may remain in backups for a limited time per the applicable retention cycle. During that period, deleted data is not used for ordinary operational purposes, access to it is restricted, backups remain subject to appropriate security controls, and they are disposed of or replaced per their normal cycle.

sections.heading: 9. Secure Deletion & Anonymization
body: ZynReach uses deletion or destruction methods appropriate to the medium and data type, which may include logical deletion, database deletion, file removal, destruction of storage media where necessary, or destruction of encryption keys where appropriate, without any commitment to using a single method for all data types.

Where appropriate, ZynReach may use anonymization instead of full deletion, provided the resulting data cannot reasonably be linked to an individual's identity under the applicable legal standard, and may use it for purposes such as statistical analysis, product improvement, research, and operational planning.

sections.heading: 10. Legally Required Data & Legal Hold
body: ZynReach may retain certain data even after its operational purpose has ended where retention is required or permitted by law, court order, accounting or tax requirements, regulatory obligations, or in connection with an actual or reasonably anticipated dispute or the exercise or defense of legal rights — retained only to the extent and for the duration necessary for that lawful purpose.

Where a dispute, investigation, or legal claim arises, ZynReach may suspend normal deletion processes for the relevant data (a "Legal Hold") until the reason for retention ends, at which point the data returns to its normal retention and deletion cycle.

sections.heading: 11. Individual Deletion Requests
body: When an individual submits a request to delete personal data, ZynReach assesses it based on the requester's identity, the nature of the data, ZynReach's role in the processing, the legal basis, the applicable agreement, and relevant laws. There may be cases where full deletion cannot be carried out, such as where retention is legally required; in those cases, processing is limited to what is necessary for the purpose preventing deletion.

sections.heading: 12. Account Data & Inactive Accounts
body: Upon closing a user's account, ZynReach may disable the account and remove login access, delete data no longer necessary, while retaining data required by law or necessary for security, fraud prevention, or the defense of legal rights.

ZynReach may apply measures to accounts inactive for extended periods (notifying the user, restricting certain functionality, suspending or closing the account, deleting or hiding certain data), in accordance with the applicable terms of service and agreements and any legal obligations.

sections.heading: 13. Marketing Data & Correspondence
body: Marketing data is managed according to the purpose and legal basis used to collect it; when a user withdraws consent, ZynReach stops sending communications that require that consent, while retaining limited information necessary to ensure marketing communications are not sent again to someone who has unsubscribed.

ZynReach may retain correspondence with customers or users for an appropriate period for customer service, dispute resolution, follow-up, and legal obligations; the end of a conversation does not mean the associated data is immediately deleted.

sections.heading: 14. System, Security & Audit Logs
body: ZynReach may retain system and security logs for a period that differs from the retention period for account or Customer Data, for purposes such as detecting attacks, investigating incidents, preventing abuse, auditing access, protecting the platform, and business continuity — these logs may be kept longer where necessary for a legitimate security or legal purpose.

Audit logs may contain information about logins, permission changes, account setting changes, administrative actions, security events, and sensitive operations; their retention period is determined based on security risk, operational need, and contractual and legal requirements.

sections.heading: 15. Sub-processors & Independent Third Parties
body: Where ZynReach uses sub-processors or external service providers, it seeks to impose appropriate requirements regarding retention, deletion, data protection, confidentiality, data return, and disposal at the end of service; these relationships are also governed by the Sub-processor Policy and the DPA.

Where a third party processes data as an independent Controller (rather than as a sub-processor acting on ZynReach's behalf), that party's data retention may be governed by its own privacy and retention policy, and ZynReach bears no responsibility for retention periods set by that independent Controller outside its legal or contractual control.

sections.heading: 16. Data Lifecycle & Classification
body: ZynReach follows a data lifecycle concept: Collection → Processing → Active Storage → Archiving/Restricted Storage → Deletion/Anonymization — not all data types necessarily pass through every stage, and the path is determined by the data's nature, purpose, risk, and legal obligations.

ZynReach may classify data by sensitivity and protection requirements (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted); the classification level may affect the retention period, access permissions, encryption requirements, logging and monitoring requirements, and the deletion mechanism used.

sections.heading: 17. Minimum Retention & Periodic Review
body: ZynReach seeks not to retain personal data longer than necessary, while acknowledging that "minimum" does not necessarily mean the shortest possible period, since law, contracts, security, accounting, fraud prevention, or legal defense may require a longer period.

ZynReach may review retention periods from time to time (upon a product change, a change in processing method, the introduction of a new system, a change in legal requirements, or a security incident), without this meaning that every category of data is reviewed at the same time.

sections.heading: 18. Internal Access & Termination of Access
body: Employees and internal users with access to ZynReach data must use it only for authorized business purposes, avoid retaining unnecessary copies or transferring data to unauthorized systems, follow internal deletion procedures, and report any loss or unauthorized disclosure.

When an employee's or contractor's access to ZynReach systems ends, their permissions are revoked or adjusted per identity and access management procedures; this does not necessarily mean the records they created are deleted, as retaining them may be necessary for audit, security, and compliance purposes.

sections.heading: 19. Temporary & Cached Data, and Technical Logs
body: Temporary or cached data may be generated while the services run, and may be deleted or replaced automatically per the technical systems used; it is not necessarily considered part of the Customer's permanent data unless the agreement states otherwise.

System logs may contain identifiers or technical information linked to users or accounts, used where necessary for operations, security, diagnostics, performance, and incident investigation, and retained per the appropriate cycle for each system.

sections.heading: 20. Multi-Phase Deletion at Service Termination & Exceptions
body: Upon service termination, ZynReach may carry out a multi-phase deletion process:
list: Disabling account access, then providing an export or retrieval mechanism where available under the agreement.
Removing data from operational systems per the DPA and agreement, then allowing the backup cycle containing the data to lapse.
Handling any data that must be legally retained, then closing the data's lifecycle.

Deletion may be suspended or delayed where necessary due to a legal obligation, court order, investigation, dispute, legal hold, security requirements, or business continuity — such an exception must not be used as a means of indefinitely retaining data without justification.

sections.heading: 21. Technical Limitations & No Guarantee of Immediate Deletion
body: ZynReach acknowledges that complete, immediate deletion across all technical systems may not always be possible, particularly in distributed environments or backup and caching systems, and deletion may accordingly be carried out on a reasonable technical cycle rather than instantaneously across every technical layer.
Unless the DPA, applicable law, or the agreement provides otherwise, ZynReach does not guarantee that data deletion will occur at the exact moment a deletion request is submitted.

sections.heading: 22. Proof of Deletion & Customer Requests
body: Where appropriate or contractually required, ZynReach may document a deletion process or maintain an internal record evidencing that it was carried out, without any obligation to issue an independent deletion certificate for every deletion unless the agreement or law requires it.

Customers may request information or clarification about retention and deletion procedures through ZynReach's official channels; a request should ideally include the company name, account details, the service concerned, the data or accounts in question, and any information necessary for verification.

body: This policy is read together with the Data Processing Agreement; in the event of a conflict, the DPA governs with respect to Customer Data, particularly regarding data return, deletion, retention, backups, and service termination.

The Privacy Policy sets out how personal data is collected, used, and disclosed, while this policy focuses on the data lifecycle and retention and deletion periods — the two documents should be read together. Data also remains subject, throughout its retention period, to the security controls set out in the Security & Trust Policy (access control, authentication, encryption, logging, monitoring, incident response).

body: ZynReach seeks to design its retention and deletion processes consistent with applicable data-protection laws, without this meaning that every legal requirement in every country applies to every customer or data type; the relevant requirements are determined by jurisdiction, the nature of the service, and the parties' roles.

ZynReach may amend this policy from time to time to reflect legal or technical developments, changes to the services, or changes to the data lifecycle, and publishes the updated version through appropriate channels. sections.heading: 4. Hacking, Cyberattacks & Unauthorized Account Access
body: Hacking systems, unauthorized access, attempting to bypass security controls, or exploiting vulnerabilities without authorization is prohibited, including credential stuffing, brute-force attacks, unauthorized privilege escalation, credential theft, distributing hacking tools for malicious purposes, or disabling or bypassing protection systems.

It is also prohibited to use another person's account without authorization, share an account in an unauthorized manner, attempt to obtain another user's password, bypass multi-factor authentication, steal session tokens, or use stolen credentials.

sections.heading: 5. Malware
body: Using ZynReach to store, distribute, or publish malware, ransomware, spyware, trojans, worms, viruses, keyloggers, botnet components, or any software designed to damage systems or steal data is prohibited.

sections.heading: 6. Phishing, Fraud & Impersonation
body: Using ZynReach to create or distribute phishing messages, fake login pages, fraudulent campaigns, credential-theft schemes, or fraudulent offers or transactions is prohibited; this applies even where the activity is presented as a "test," unless properly authorized with a clear scope.

Impersonating an individual, company, government entity, financial institution, employee, customer, or brand is also prohibited, as is using ZynReach to create a misleading impression that a user represents ZynReach or Zyntra Digital without authorization.

sections.heading: 7. Spam & Unsolicited Messages
body: Using ZynReach to send or facilitate the sending of unsolicited bulk messages, fraudulent messages, messages that violate applicable law, or messages sent without an appropriate legal basis is prohibited; users must comply with consent, opt-out, and marketing-list management requirements applicable to their activity.

sections.heading: 8. Resource Abuse, Rate Limits & Denial-of-Service
body: Unreasonable resource consumption, running operations that affect service performance, attempting to exhaust resources, generating an abnormal volume of requests, or bypassing technical limits or rate limits is prohibited; ZynReach may apply technical usage limits to protect the service.
Using ZynReach to carry out or facilitate denial-of-service attacks (DoS/DDoS), traffic flooding, resource exhaustion, or any activity intended to disrupt a service or system is also prohibited.

sections.heading: 9. Security Scanning & Penetration Testing
body: Port scanning, vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, or automated security testing may not be performed on ZynReach's systems unless authorized in writing, part of a formal security program, or expressly permitted by ZynReach, and must comply with any scope or testing rules the Company specifies.

sections.heading: 10. Unlawful Data Collection & Sensitive Data
body: Using ZynReach to collect, extract, or process personal data in a manner that violates applicable law is prohibited; the Customer is responsible for ensuring an appropriate lawful basis exists for data it enters or collects through the service.

ZynReach must not be used to process special or highly sensitive categories of data unless the feature is suitable for that purpose, the agreement permits it, the use is lawful, and the required safeguards are applied.

sections.heading: 11. Unlawful Content & Intellectual Property
body: Using ZynReach to store, distribute, or publish content that is unlawful under applicable law is prohibited; ZynReach may take action upon receiving a credible notice or discovering unlawful activity, per appropriate procedures.

ZynReach may not be used to infringe copyrights, trademarks, or patents, steal trade secrets, or distribute content the user does not have the right to distribute; the user is responsible for ensuring it holds the necessary licenses for content it uploads or processes.

sections.heading: 12. Privacy Violations & Financial Information
body: Using ZynReach to monitor individuals without a lawful basis, collect personal data without authorization, publish personal data without a lawful basis, disclose private information, or use personal data for unauthorized purposes is prohibited.

ZynReach may not be used to store or process sensitive financial information unless the service and agreement permit it, and the Customer must comply with regulatory requirements relating to financial data and payments where applicable.

sections.heading: 13. Harmful Content & High-Risk Uses
body: Using ZynReach in a manner intended to cause physical, digital, or financial harm to others is prohibited, including malware, fraud tools, identity-theft campaigns, and digital extortion.

ZynReach may not be used in high-risk applications where failure could cause serious harm (such as critical medical or industrial-control systems, emergency systems, or military systems, or any system whose failure could pose a direct risk to life or safety), unless ZynReach has expressly agreed under special terms.

sections.heading: 14. Artificial Intelligence
body: Where ZynReach offers AI-powered functionality, it may not be used to produce fraudulent content, impersonate identities, bypass security controls, automate harmful activity, make unlawful decisions about individuals, or process data the user lacks the right to use; the user remains responsible for verifying the suitability and legality of using AI outputs.

sections.heading: 15. Automation, Web Scraping & Trial Accounts
body: Automation, APIs, and scripts may be used where supported and permitted by ZynReach; automation that exceeds limits, affects the service, misleadingly mimics users, extracts unreasonable amounts of data, or bypasses protection mechanisms is prohibited.

ZynReach may not be used for scraping or extraction purposes in a manner that exceeds technical restrictions or rate limits, violates others' rights, or unlawfully collects personal data. Where ZynReach provides trial accounts, they must be used only for legitimate purposes; creating a large number of them to exceed limits, exhaust resources, or obtain services without payment is prohibited.

sections.heading: 16. Login Credentials & Customer Responsibility for Users
body: Users must keep login credentials confidential, not share passwords or API keys, and not publish access tokens; the Customer is responsible for activity conducted through its accounts to the extent provided by the agreement and applicable law.

Where the Customer is an organization, it is responsible for taking appropriate steps to ensure its users comply with this policy, including managing accounts and permissions, revoking unauthorized users' access, educating users, and monitoring usage where necessary.

sections.heading: 17. User-Submitted Content & No Implied Consent
body: ZynReach is not responsible for content the Customer or a user enters merely by hosting or processing it, unless the law or the agreement provides otherwise; the user is responsible for the content's legality, its usage rights, its accuracy, and ensuring it does not infringe others' rights or violate this policy.

ZynReach's failure to act against a given use at a given time does not mean that use is always permitted, that the Company has approved it, that the Company has waived its rights, or that it will not take action in the future.

sections.heading: 18. Security Monitoring & Investigation of Violations
body: ZynReach may use technical systems to monitor performance, security, abnormal activity, abuse, hacking attempts, and resource consumption, in accordance with the Privacy Policy and applicable law.

Where there is reasonable cause to suspect a violation of this policy, ZynReach may conduct an appropriate investigation, which may include reviewing logs and accounts, analyzing activity, examining requests, communicating with the Customer, and engaging experts where necessary.

sections.heading: 19. Suspension of Accounts & Emergency Action
body: Where there is a security risk or material breach, ZynReach may, to the extent permitted by the agreement and applicable law, suspend an account or a specific feature, restrict access, disable an API, block a particular activity, terminate sessions, or take temporary protective measures.

ZynReach may take immediate action without prior notice where reasonably necessary to protect the platform, users, customers, data, infrastructure, or third parties, providing subsequent notice where appropriate and permitted.

sections.heading: 20. Content Removal & Government Requests
body: Where permitted or legally or contractually required, ZynReach may restrict access to certain content, disable a link, remove content from the service interface, or suspend the associated account — this does not mean ZynReach assumes general responsibility for monitoring all content.

ZynReach may take action in response to a court order, a valid legal request from a competent government authority, or regulatory requirements, in accordance with applicable law; the Customer must, to the extent required by the agreement and law, cooperate with ZynReach in investigations relating to service misuse, security incidents, or fraud.

sections.heading: 21. Reporting Abuse & False Reports
body: Use suspected of violating this policy can be reported through ZynReach's official contact channels; a report should ideally include the nature of the violation, the account or service concerned if known, the date and time, a description of the activity, available evidence, and the reporter's contact information.

The abuse-reporting mechanism may not be used to submit malicious reports, claims the submitter knows to be false, attempts to harass users, or attempts to disrupt competitors' accounts; ZynReach may disregard or take appropriate action regarding reports that appear abusive or made in bad faith.

sections.heading: 22. Vulnerability Reporting
body: Security vulnerabilities should preferably be reported through ZynReach's official responsible-disclosure channel; a vulnerability may not be exploited for malicious purposes or used to extract data unrelated to verifying the vulnerability.

sections.heading: 23. Relationship to Other Policies
body: This policy complements ZynReach's security policies: the Security & Trust Policy sets out the controls the Company uses to protect the services, while this document sets out what is and is not acceptable from users. Any processing of personal data by ZynReach is governed by the applicable Privacy Policy, and this policy does not grant ZynReach authority beyond what the law, the Privacy Policy, or the agreement permits.

Where the Customer is the Controller and ZynReach acts as Processor, obligations relating to the processing of Customer Data are also governed by the Data Processing Agreement, whose provisions govern in the event of conflict. This policy forms an integral part of the Terms of Service; in case of conflict, the Terms of Service govern to the extent specified in the agreement, unless mandatory law provides otherwise.

sections.heading: 24. Enforcement Actions & Factors Considered
body: ZynReach may take appropriate action when this policy is violated, which may include:
list: Warning the user, requesting correction of the activity, restricting use, or suspending the account or service.
Disabling an API, removing or restricting content, terminating the account, blocking future access, or taking legal action where necessary.

The action chosen depends on the severity and frequency of the violation, its impact on others, whether it was intentional, whether fraud or a security risk is involved, the user's cooperation and account history, and legal requirements; ZynReach is not obligated to follow a fixed sequence of escalating actions and may take immediate or severe action where necessary to protect users, data, the service, or infrastructure.

sections.heading: 25. Service Restoration & Third-Party Responsibility
body: If an account is suspended for a violation, ZynReach may restore service once it determines the risk has been contained, the violation has been corrected, the account is secure, and contractual and legal requirements permit it; there is no obligation to restore an account where termination is justified under the agreement or applicable law.

ZynReach may not be used in a manner that damages a third party's systems or services, and the user remains responsible for its conduct toward external systems even where the activity was carried out through ZynReach.

sections.heading: 26. Commercial Restrictions, Resale & Trademark Use
body: Using ZynReach to circumvent subscription plans, pricing, or usage limits is prohibited, including creating multiple accounts to circumvent limits, reselling the service without authorization, sharing a commercial account in violation of the plan's terms, or exceeding user limits. ZynReach may not be resold, licensed, or provided as an independent service except under a formal agreement or program ZynReach permits.
The ZynReach name, logo, the Zyntra Digital name, or related trademarks may not be used in a way that implies a relationship, endorsement, partnership, or affiliation that does not exist.

sections.heading: 27. Limits of ZynReach's Liability
body: ZynReach cannot guarantee that all users will comply with this policy, and each user remains responsible for its own use of the service. To the extent permitted by law and the agreement, ZynReach is not responsible for unlawful use by the Customer, content a user uploads, damages resulting from sharing login credentials, API misuse by the Customer, or damages arising from systems or services outside ZynReach's control.

Security violations or abuse must be reported through official channels; passwords, API keys, tokens, payment card data, or unnecessary confidential information should never be sent through public reporting channels.

sections.heading: 28. Amendments to This Policy & Their Effect
body: ZynReach may amend this policy from time to time to reflect technical developments, new security risks, legal changes, service changes, or lessons learned from incidents; the updated version is published through appropriate official channels.

Unless the agreement or law provides otherwise, amendments take effect upon publication or on the date specified in the updated version, and continued use of the service after an amendment takes effect is subject to the updated policy to the extent permitted by law.

sections.heading: 29. Order of Precedence, Severability & No Waiver
body: In the event of a conflict, the following order applies: mandatory applicable law, then a signed written agreement, then the Terms of Service/master agreement, then the Data Processing Agreement with respect to Customer Data, then this policy — applied only to the extent an actual conflict exists.

If any provision of this policy is found invalid or unenforceable in a given jurisdiction, it is construed or modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, without affecting the remaining provisions; ZynReach's failure to enforce any provision at a given time does not constitute a waiver of its right to enforce it later.

sections.heading: 30. Contact & Legal Notice
body: For questions relating to the Acceptable Use Policy or to report misuse of the services, ZynReach's official contact channels published on its website, or those specified in the agreement with the Customer, should be used.

This document represents ZynReach's general Acceptable Use Policy and is not an exhaustive list of every prohibited use; ZynReach reserves the right to take appropriate action against any use that poses a reasonable risk to platform security, data integrity, service stability, users, customers, third parties, or legal compliance. This policy does not grant ZynReach unlimited rights to monitor or access customer content, nor does it relieve users of their legal and contractual responsibilities. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. sections.heading: 1. Introduction
body: As an enterprise platform for growth, automation, and data operations, ZynReach is committed to security and organizational practices and controls designed to protect customer information, user data, and platform resources from unauthorized access, unlawful use, unauthorized alteration, loss, or disruption. ZynReach's security philosophy rests on "Security and Trust by Design" — security, trust, and data protection are core elements of how the platform is designed and operated, not add-ons applied afterward.

ZynReach applies a multi-layered approach that combines, depending on the nature of the service and environment, infrastructure security, data encryption, identity and access management, least privilege, multi-factor authentication, continuous monitoring, audit logs, vulnerability management, backup and recovery, incident response, vendor management, data protection and privacy, and governance and accountability.

sections.heading: 2. Purpose of the Policy
body: This policy sets out the general principles and controls ZynReach applies to protect customer data, personal data, user accounts, organization data, transaction and operational data, documents and files, integration data, system logs, infrastructure, systems and applications, security secrets and keys, and confidential and commercial information — and to clarify ZynReach's responsibilities and those of customers and users under a shared-responsibility model.

sections.heading: 3. Scope of the Policy
body: This policy applies, as relevant to the service, to the ZynReach platform, its applications and APIs, databases, cloud infrastructure, integration services, authentication systems, monitoring systems, logging and audit systems, backup systems, support tools, and incident-management systems, as well as vendors and sub-processors, and employees and contractors with access to ZynReach environments and data processed on customers' behalf.

sections.heading: 4. Security & Trust Principles
body: ZynReach relies on the following principles:
list: Security by Design: security requirements are considered throughout the design, development, and operation of the services. Least Privilege: access is granted only to the extent necessary to perform an authorized task.

Defense in Depth: protection does not rely on a single security control but on multiple layers. Zero Trust Principles: access to sensitive resources is treated on the basis of verification and authorization, not default trust.
Accountability: sensitive activities must be traceable and auditable where possible. Privacy by Design: data protection is considered when designing processes that handle personal data.
Continuous Improvement: security controls and practices are subject to ongoing review and improvement.

sections.heading: 5. Information Classification
body: ZynReach may classify information into the following levels: Public (information that can be released publicly), Internal (for internal use), Confidential (non-public commercial or operational information), Restricted (sensitive security or technical information), and Highly Restricted (information whose disclosure could pose a material security or business risk) — the appropriate level of protection is determined based on the nature of the information and its associated risks.

sections.heading: 6. Protection of Customer Data
body: ZynReach treats customer data as among the most important assets requiring protection; controls include, depending on the service and environment, access control, encryption, activity logging, separation of duties, access monitoring, backups, restoration procedures, incident management, vulnerability management, and infrastructure protection.

ZynReach personnel may not access customer data unless access is necessary for a legitimate function, authorized, consistent with approved permissions, and subject to appropriate controls; internal access to customer data is determined by role and logged.

sections.heading: 7. Encryption
body: Appropriate encryption protocols, including TLS, are used to protect data while it is in transit between the user and the platform or between systems requiring a secure connection; ZynReach uses appropriate encryption to protect stored data consistent with the service's technical architecture, and backups are subject to appropriate security controls to protect them from unauthorized access or use.

sections.heading: 8. Identity & Access Management
body: ZynReach applies controls to verify that a user or system attempting to access a resource holds the appropriate permission; these controls may include authentication, authorization, role- or attribute-based access control, multi-factor authentication, session controls, privileged access management, access reviews, and audit logging — role/attribute-based access control is applied to actions, with a complete audit log of access to customer data.

sections.heading: 9. Multi-Factor Authentication
body: ZynReach supports multi-factor authentication depending on the account level, plan, and function; it is available for every account and required for administrative and Enterprise roles using time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). Customers must protect their authentication factors, not share verification codes, use trusted authentication methods, and remove access methods when a user leaves the organization.

sections.heading: 10. Privilege Management & Administrative Access
body: ZynReach applies the principle that access is granted based on business need; users and employees are not assumed to have unnecessary access to data or systems. The permission-management process includes requesting access, administrator approval, defining the role, granting the permission, reviewing it, modifying it, and revoking it once no longer needed.

Access to sensitive systems and resources is subject to additional controls, including identifying authorized users, separation of duties, activity logging, permission reviews, access restrictions, strong authentication, and revoking permissions once no longer needed.

sections.heading: 11. Audit Logging & Log Integrity
body: Audit logs are a core part of ZynReach's governance and security model; important activities are logged in a way that allows understanding who took an action, what the action was, when it occurred, and on which resource — platform actions (including record changes, approvals, logins, and settings) are recorded in a searchable audit trail.

ZynReach aims to protect audit logs from unauthorized modification, deletion, or access, and uses them for security, investigation, governance, troubleshooting, compliance, and activity review purposes.

sections.heading: 12. Secure Software Development
body: ZynReach adopts practices intended to build security into the software development lifecycle, which may include security-requirements review, code review, dependency and vulnerability scanning, secrets management, application testing, change review, version control, and environment separation — without this meaning any software can be guaranteed absolutely free of vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: 13. Vulnerability Management
body: ZynReach uses practices to manage technical vulnerabilities and risk, including discovery, risk assessment, prioritization, remediation, fix verification, follow-up, and closure, with continuous vulnerability scanning and periodic third-party security assessments.

sections.heading: 14. Security Testing
body: Depending on the scope of the service and environment, ZynReach conducts security tests and assessments (vulnerability assessments, security testing, third-party security assessments, infrastructure or application reviews) intended to identify risks and improve controls; the results of any particular test do not constitute a guarantee that the platform is free of all risk.

sections.heading: 15. Security Monitoring
body: ZynReach monitors systems and activities relevant to security and operations, using alerting mechanisms when unusual behavior or activity is detected, including continuous monitoring of infrastructure and access activity and alerting on unusual behavior.

sections.heading: 16. Security Incident Management
body: ZynReach maintains a framework for responding to security incidents, including detection, initial triage, severity classification, containment, investigation, remediation, service restoration, and post-incident review; it has a documented incident-response plan with severity levels, escalation, and customer-notification processes consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.

sections.heading: 17. Customer Incident Notification
body: Where a security incident affects Customer data, it is handled according to its nature, scope, severity, legal and contractual obligations, and applicable regulatory requirements; not every technical alert or internal security event constitutes an incident requiring customer notification — whether notification is required is determined based on assessment of the incident and applicable law or contract.

sections.heading: 18. Backup, Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity
body: ZynReach uses regular automated backup processes consistent with the service's operational architecture, aimed at protecting data, supporting restoration, reducing the impact of incidents, and supporting service continuity, with documented recovery and restoration procedures; the existence of disaster-recovery procedures does not guarantee that all services will resume at a specific time under all circumstances, unless expressly agreed in an SLA or Enterprise agreement.

ZynReach seeks to maintain the continuity of core services through contingency planning, monitoring, backups, restoration procedures, operational escalation, and incident management; continuity objectives and service levels may vary by plan and agreement.

sections.heading: 19. Infrastructure Security
body: ZynReach relies on infrastructure and technology providers to support platform operations; controls include access control, encryption, system monitoring, configuration management, vulnerability management, backups, and activity logging. Customer data is hosted by default in data centers within the United States, with regional options available for Enterprise plans as contractually available.

sections.heading: 20. Sub-processors & Vendor Risk Management
body: ZynReach may use third parties to provide services necessary to operate the platform (cloud infrastructure, email delivery, analytics, customer support), and the sub-processor list is updated consistent with the Data Processing Agreement.

ZynReach seeks to assess the risks associated with vendors and external services based on the importance of the service and the nature of the data involved, which may include security assessment, privacy assessment, contractual review, service-level review, and review of data-protection requirements.

sections.heading: 21. Data Protection, Privacy & Data Minimization
body: ZynReach treats data protection as a core element of trust; when acting as a data processor on a customer's behalf, processing is governed by the Data Processing Agreement, the service agreement, and applicable law, which provide for processing based on the customer's documented instructions, with provisions relating to sub-processors, security measures, data subject rights, and international transfers.

ZynReach seeks not to collect or process information beyond what is necessary for the service's legitimate purposes, where possible and appropriate; the customer remains responsible for determining the type of data it enters into the platform and ensuring it has the necessary lawful basis to process it.

sections.heading: 22. Data Retention & International Transfers
body: Data retention periods are subject to the nature of the data, service settings, the agreement, the DPA, legal requirements, and restoration and backup needs; deleting data from the user interface does not necessarily mean all associated backup copies are deleted at the same moment, as backups may be subject to defined technical retention cycles.

Where personal data is transferred across borders, ZynReach applies appropriate legal safeguards under applicable law, and the current DPA provides for appropriate safeguards when conducting international transfers of personal data.

sections.heading: 23. Personnel Security & Access Termination
body: Employees and contractors with access to sensitive information or systems are subject to appropriate controls depending on their roles, including defined responsibilities, confidentiality agreements, training, permission management, access review, and revocation of access once no longer needed.

When an employee's or contractor's relationship ends or their role changes, appropriate steps are taken to revoke or adjust permissions per internal processes, to prevent continued unnecessary access to systems or data.

sections.heading: 24. Integration, API & AI Security
body: ZynReach supports integration with external systems and services, including APIs and webhooks; credentials for integrations must be protected using appropriate security practices, and ZynReach is not responsible for the compromise of an external account or system resulting from the customer's or a third party's mismanagement of credentials.

Because ZynReach includes AI capabilities (Assistants, Agents, and Insights), intelligent systems are treated as part of the security and governance environment; AI operations are subject, depending on the feature, to principles of access control, data minimization, human oversight, auditability, approval controls, guardrails, and appropriate authorization. AI Agents can perform real actions, with human-approval checkpoints and an audit log for every action; AI outputs may not be interpreted as a final legal, financial, or security decision unless approved by the user or an authorized party.

sections.heading: 25. Shared Responsibility Model
body: Service security is a shared responsibility between ZynReach and the customer. ZynReach's responsibilities include, depending on the service, platform security, infrastructure security, system protection, vulnerability management, monitoring, incident response, and backups. The customer's responsibilities include protecting login credentials, managing users and permissions, choosing authorized users, protecting devices used for access and integration keys, defining the data it enters, and complying with laws relating to its data.

ZynReach cannot control every risk existing on a customer's devices, networks, or external systems; the customer must therefore take appropriate measures such as using up-to-date devices, protecting accounts, enabling multi-factor authentication, preventing account sharing, using secure networks, training employees, and monitoring users.

sections.heading: 26. Vulnerability Disclosure & Unauthorized Testing
body: ZynReach encourages security researchers and customers to responsibly report potential vulnerabilities via security@zynreach.com, without exploiting the vulnerability, accessing customer data, modifying data, disrupting the service, or conducting broad tests without authorization, while providing the information necessary to help the security team understand and verify the issue.

Publishing this policy or any security documentation does not constitute authorization to conduct penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, exploitation, load testing, or reverse engineering on ZynReach's systems; prior written authorization must be obtained before any security test beyond normal authorized use.

sections.heading: 27. Compliance & Security Frameworks
body: ZynReach seeks to align its security program with frameworks appropriate to the nature of its services, and currently addresses SOC 2 Type II (security, availability, and confidentiality controls with independent audit), ISO 27001 (information security management practices aligned with the framework), GDPR (data-processing practices designed to support relevant requirements), and CCPA (California consumer-privacy rights and disclosures) — with the scope of each framework set out separately on the Compliance page.

Referencing any standard, framework, or law does not mean that using ZynReach automatically makes the customer compliant with all of its requirements; compliance also depends on how the customer uses the service, the type of data, the location of the parties, the industry, internal procedures, the legal basis for processing, and system settings. ZynReach is committed to making its security and compliance claims verifiable and clearly scoped, without using terms like "certified," "compliant," "audited," "aligned," or "ready" interchangeably.

sections.heading: 28. Security Documentation & Confidentiality
body: Qualified customers may request additional documentation under the Security & Compliance Documentation Request Policy, including a security whitepaper, security questionnaire, technical and organizational measures, incident-response overview, business-continuity and disaster-recovery overviews, sub-processor and data-residency information, and encryption and access-control overviews; submitting a request does not mean all documentation will automatically be provided.

Because security documentation may contain sensitive information, ZynReach reserves the right to decline a request, redact parts of a document, provide a summary, require an NDA, verify the requester's identity, or restrict redistribution, in order to prevent security information from being used in a way that could increase risk to the platform or its customers.

sections.heading: 29. No Absolute Security Guarantee & Limitation of Liability
