body: Despite taking appropriate technical and organizational measures, no information system can be absolutely immune to all risk; accordingly, ZynReach does not guarantee that the service will be free of all vulnerabilities, that all attacks will be prevented, that the service will not experience any interruption, or that no security incident or data loss will occur under all circumstances — specific guarantees are subject to applicable commercial agreements, SLAs, and the DPA.

This policy does not create any independent contractual liability beyond that set out in the applicable commercial agreement or Terms of Service; no security description in this document should be interpreted as an absolute guarantee, insurance against loss, a commitment to a specific security outcome, or a waiver of any contractual right.

sections.heading: 30. Amendments & Relationship to Other Documents
body: ZynReach reserves the right to update this policy where a material change occurs in the service, technical architecture, legal requirements, security frameworks, or vendor processes, or where new risks emerge or security controls are improved; the last-updated date will be noted in the published version.

This policy is read together with the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Data Processing Agreement, Security & Compliance Documentation Request Policy, Sub-processor Policy, Data Retention Policy, Incident Response Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, and, where applicable, an Enterprise Agreement or SLA; in the event of conflict, precedence follows the applicable contractual agreements and applicable law.

sections.heading: 31. Intellectual Property
body: All content of this policy and related security documentation, including text, graphics, and methodologies, is owned by or licensed to ZynReach, and viewing it does not transfer any intellectual-property rights.

sections.heading: 32. Contact & Security Notification
body: Security inquiries: security@zynreach.com. Legal inquiries: legal@zynreach.com. Privacy inquiries: privacy@zynreach.com. To request Enterprise documentation: via the Security & Compliance Documentation Request Policy.

If a user or customer discovers a real or potential security issue, its details should not be publicly disclosed before ZynReach has had a reasonable opportunity to verify and address it; a report sent to security@zynreach.com should ideally describe the issue, the affected systems, reproduction steps if possible, and the expected level of impact, without sending personal or customer data not necessary for the investigation.

sections.heading: 33. Our Commitment to Trust
body: ZynReach seeks to build a long-term relationship with its customers based on security, privacy, transparency, and accountability; trust is not merely a marketing phrase but the result of practices and controls that can be reviewed and verified within the scope of the service.

sections.heading: 34. Legal Disclaimer
body: This document provides a general description of ZynReach's security and trust framework and does not constitute legal advice, an independent contractual commitment, or an absolute guarantee of security or compliance, and does not replace commercial agreements, the Terms of Use, the Data Processing Agreement, the SLA, or a customer's own legal requirements; where a specific commitment exists between ZynReach and a customer, the written and effective contractual commitment is the governing reference. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

incident-response.title: Incident Response & Security Breach Notification Policy

sections.heading: 1. Purpose of the Policy
body: This policy sets out the framework ZynReach follows for handling security incidents, suspected data breaches, and cyber incidents that may affect ZynReach's systems or the data processed through them, with the aim of detecting and reporting incidents, assessing their nature and scope, containing and limiting their effects, investigating their causes, preserving evidence, and safely restoring systems.

The policy also aims to determine whether an incident constitutes a security breach or a personal data breach under applicable law, carry out notifications required by law or contract, communicate appropriately with customers and affected parties, and take corrective action to prevent recurrence.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of the Policy
body: This policy applies to incidents that may affect the ZynReach website and platform, technical infrastructure, databases, storage systems, administrative and user accounts, APIs, third-party services, sub-processors, email and communication systems, backups, and internal systems related to service delivery.

It applies to incidents arising from cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data leaks, data loss, accidental disclosure, malware, phishing, account compromise, privilege misuse, human or software errors, system misconfiguration, security vulnerabilities, or incidents at service providers, or any other event that could materially affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information.

sections.heading: 3. Definitions
list: Security Incident: any event or set of events that may affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems, information, or services.
Security Breach: a security incident that resulted, or could reasonably result, in unauthorized access to, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of information or systems.
Personal Data Breach: a security breach leading to the destruction, loss, alteration, disclosure, or unauthorized access to personal data, to the extent this definition applies under applicable law.

Incident Response Team: the individuals or teams ZynReach designates to manage and respond to security incidents. Containment: measures taken to contain an incident and prevent it from spreading. Recovery: procedures to restore systems, data, and services to a safe operating state.

sections.heading: 4. Core Incident Response Principles
body: ZynReach follows these principles:
list: Speed: seeking to detect and respond to incidents as quickly as practicable. Accuracy: not issuing final conclusions before sufficient information is available, where the nature of the incident allows.
Harm minimization: prioritizing containment and reducing impact. Evidence protection: seeking to preserve technical information and evidence necessary for investigation.
Confidentiality: restricting incident-related information on a need-to-know basis. Compliance: managing incidents consistent with relevant legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 5. Incident Response Lifecycle
body: ZynReach follows a response lifecycle that may include: Detection → Triage → Assessment → Containment → Investigation → Eradication → Recovery → Notification → Post-Incident Review — certain stages may be skipped or combined depending on the nature of the incident.

sections.heading: 6. Detecting & Reporting Incidents
body: Incidents may be detected through security monitoring systems, audit logs, alerts, vulnerability detection, or reports from employees, customers, users, service providers, sub-processors, security researchers, government authorities, or other trusted sources; an alert or the detection of unusual activity does not necessarily mean a security breach has actually occurred.

ZynReach encourages employees, users, customers, and service providers to report suspicious security activity as quickly as practicable — such as an unrecognized login, lost credentials, phishing messages, unauthorized access, accidental data disclosure, abnormal system behavior, or loss of a device containing sensitive information.

sections.heading: 7. Initial Incident Assessment
body: Upon receiving a report or detecting an incident, ZynReach assesses the nature of the event, the systems and data affected, whether personal data or Customer Data is involved, the extent of unauthorized access, the number of users or customers potentially affected, the likelihood of harm, whether the incident is ongoing, the need for immediate containment, and potential legal or contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 8. Incident Severity Classification
body: ZynReach may classify incidents into four levels:
list: Level 1 — Low: a limited incident that does not materially affect systems or data (an unconfirmed alert, a failed access attempt, suspicious activity contained with no known impact).
Level 2 — Medium: an incident with limited impact on a specific system, service, or accounts.
Level 3 — High: an incident that may affect important data or service, or a number of customers.

Level 4 — Critical: a broad or material incident that may affect Customer Data, personal data, the confidentiality or integrity of data, the availability of the service significantly, a large number of customers, or core infrastructure; classification may be adjusted during the investigation as new information emerges.

sections.heading: 9. Incident Response Team & Authority
body: ZynReach may assemble an incident response team suited to the nature of the incident, which may include security, engineering, infrastructure/DevOps, IT, privacy, legal, management, customer success, and communications functions, and may engage external experts or consultants where needed.

The team may, to the extent necessary and authorized, disable an account, terminate sessions, change credentials, isolate a system, restrict access, block suspicious traffic, temporarily suspend an affected service, or apply emergency security measures; containment actions may temporarily affect certain services where necessary to protect systems or data.

sections.heading: 10. Containment & Technical Investigation
body: ZynReach seeks to contain incidents through measures such as isolating systems, disabling compromised accounts, rotating access keys, terminating sessions, blocking malicious sources, restricting permissions, and disabling an affected component; the specific action is chosen based on risk and circumstances.

Following initial containment, ZynReach investigates to determine how and when the incident began, the systems and data affected, the scope of access, the duration of exposure, whether the attacker still has access, actions already taken, and measures needed to prevent recurrence — it may not be possible to determine every detail of an incident immediately.

sections.heading: 11. Preservation of Evidence & Eradication
body: Where appropriate, ZynReach seeks to preserve relevant evidence (logs, audit trails, system events, network information, authentication records) in a manner appropriate to the nature of the incident and legal requirements.

After understanding the root cause, ZynReach works, where possible, to remove or address the source of the incident by fixing the vulnerability, updating the system, revoking inappropriate permissions, rotating keys or credentials, removing malware, or updating monitoring rules.

sections.heading: 12. Service Restoration
body: After containing an incident and eradicating its cause, ZynReach works to safely restore systems, including verifying system integrity, confirming the threat is no longer active, restoring data where needed, testing services, gradually reactivating systems, and increasing monitoring after restoration.

sections.heading: 13. Assessing Whether an Incident Is a Data Breach
body: Not every security incident constitutes a personal data breach; ZynReach assesses whether the incident resulted, or could reasonably result, in unauthorized access to, disclosure of, loss, alteration, or destruction of personal data, or an effect on individuals' rights or freedoms where that is a criterion under applicable law — the legal classification is determined based on the law and the actual circumstances of the incident.

sections.heading: 14. Customer Notification & Phased Notification
body: Where ZynReach is contractually or legally obligated to notify a customer of a breach relating to its data, it seeks to provide notice per the timeframe and mechanism set out in the DPA or applicable agreement, including, to the extent available, a general description of the incident, the date the incident occurred and was discovered, systems and data categories affected, containment and remedial measures, and a point of contact.

Not all information may be available when an incident is discovered; ZynReach may accordingly send an initial notice with information available at that time, followed by updates as material additional information becomes available, without waiting for the investigation to conclude where early notification is legally or contractually required.

sections.heading: 15. Notification Content & Timing
body: ZynReach seeks to ensure notifications are as accurate and clear as possible, based on available information, proportionate to the nature of the incident, and free of unconfirmed speculation, without including details that could endanger system security, reveal trade secrets, assist an attacker, disclose other customers' information, hinder the investigation, or be legally prohibited.

ZynReach complies with deadlines imposed by law or applicable agreements where they apply; where no specific deadline exists, it seeks to provide notice within a reasonable period given the nature of the incident, its scope, the level of certainty available, and legal and contractual requirements.

sections.heading: 16. Notification on Behalf of the Customer & Regulatory Notification
body: Where ZynReach acts as a Processor on the customer's behalf, the customer may be the party legally responsible for notifying data subjects and regulators; ZynReach does not do so on the customer's behalf except where legally required, contractually authorized, or requested by the customer where circumstances and law permit.

Where ZynReach is itself legally responsible for reporting to a regulatory or government authority, it assesses reporting requirements under applicable law (the competent authority, type of notice, deadline, required information, submission mechanism) based on jurisdiction and the nature of the incident; where legally obligated to notify data subjects directly, it assesses the level of risk, nature of the data, likelihood of harm, and available means of contact.

sections.heading: 17. Public Communications & Investigation Confidentiality
body: Public statements about a security incident may only be issued by authorized individuals or functions, coordinated with management, legal, security, privacy, and communications teams, avoiding the release of information that could expose ZynReach or its customers to further risk.

ZynReach treats security investigations as sensitive information, and may restrict access to incident details, evidence, the names of affected individuals, customer information, and preliminary investigation findings on a need-to-know basis.

sections.heading: 18. Incidents at Sub-processors
body: Where a security incident occurs at a sub-processor that affects or may affect data processed on behalf of ZynReach or its customers, ZynReach works to obtain available information, assess the impact, identify affected data, assess risk, take appropriate containment measures, and carry out notifications required under the DPA and applicable law; managing such cases is also governed by the Sub-processor Policy.

sections.heading: 19. Account-Related Incidents & Customer Responsibility
body: Where a user account is compromised or suspected of compromise, ZynReach may suspend the account, terminate active sessions, reset login credentials, require additional authentication, request identity verification, review activity, and notify the user where necessary.

The customer is responsible for protecting its own login credentials, managing its users, using strong passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication where available, not sharing login credentials, and reporting suspicious activity; ZynReach is not responsible for an incident resulting exclusively from the customer's or its users' conduct, to the extent permitted by law and the agreement.

sections.heading: 20. Cooperation with the Customer & Cost of Response
body: Where an incident affects Customer Data, ZynReach provides, to a reasonable and available extent and consistent with the DPA, information about the incident, appropriate technical cooperation, and information necessary for compliance, without any obligation to provide confidential information or trade secrets not otherwise required by law or contract.

Each party bears the response costs that fall within its own responsibility under law and the agreement; ZynReach does not bear the cost of special measures or additional investigations requested by the customer unless required under the agreement or law, or otherwise agreed.

sections.heading: 21. External Experts & Law Enforcement
body: ZynReach may engage cybersecurity experts, legal advisors, digital forensics specialists, and incident-response service providers where it considers appropriate to the nature of the incident.

It may cooperate with government or law enforcement authorities where legally required, necessary for the investigation, or appropriate to protect customers or users, and where permitted by law; information provided may be limited to what is legally required.

sections.heading: 22. Damage Assessment & Corrective Actions
body: ZynReach may assess the number of individuals affected, the types and sensitivity of the data, the duration of exposure, the likelihood of misuse, the impact on the service, and legal and operational risks; the existence of an incident does not mean actual harm has occurred to every potentially affected person or customer.

After an incident concludes, ZynReach may implement corrective actions such as fixing vulnerabilities, updating systems, adjusting permissions, improving monitoring, strengthening authentication, improving backup procedures, updating policies, training employees, and improving vendor management and response procedures.

sections.heading: 23. Post-Incident Review & Records
body: Following significant incidents, ZynReach may conduct a post-incident review to determine what happened, why it happened, what was discovered, how the response was carried out, what worked, what needs improvement, and lessons learned.

ZynReach may retain incident records (date, source of the report, classification, affected systems, containment measures, investigation findings, notifications, corrective actions), subject to its applicable data-retention policies.

sections.heading: 24. Testing the Response Plan & Relationship to Business Continuity
body: ZynReach may test its incident-response procedures through tabletop exercises, restoration tests, security tests, incident simulations, and business-continuity tests, using the results to improve response procedures where needed.

This policy complements ZynReach's business-continuity and disaster-recovery procedures: while this policy focuses on responding to security incidents, continuity and recovery plans focus on restoring services and data, minimizing downtime, and maintaining ongoing operations.

sections.heading: 25. Limits of Commitment & No Admission of Liability
body: ZynReach does not guarantee the prevention of all security incidents, the immediate detection of every incident, the immediate determination of every incident's details, the prevention of all effects of incidents, or the elimination of all cyber risk; the effectiveness of the response also depends on the nature of the threat, the systems affected, third-party information, and the cooperation available.

No notification, cooperation, or action ZynReach takes in relation to a security incident constitutes an admission of legal liability, an admission of negligence, or a waiver of any legal defense, contractual right, or an admission that all data has been accessed or disclosed; liability is determined based on the facts, the agreement, and applicable law.

sections.heading: 26. Protecting Sensitive Information & Handling Vulnerabilities
body: ZynReach may withhold or limit the disclosure of certain incident-related information where disclosure could expose systems to further risk, reveal unpatched vulnerabilities, help an attack recur, disclose trade secrets or other parties' information, hinder the investigation, or violate the law.

Not every security vulnerability constitutes a security incident or data breach; ZynReach assesses vulnerabilities based on risk level, exploitability, and potential impact, and may log, classify, prioritize, remediate, monitor, and notify affected parties regarding a vulnerability where required.

sections.heading: 27. Responsible Disclosure & Staff Obligations
body: ZynReach encourages security researchers to responsibly report vulnerabilities that may affect its services, and may publish or operate an independent vulnerability-reporting program with specific requirements for testing scope, communication methods, and disclosure.

Employees and contractors must promptly report suspected incidents, avoid investigating in a manner that could destroy evidence, not share incident details with unauthorized parties, follow the response team's instructions, protect customer data, and comply with security and privacy policies.

sections.heading: 28. Policy Review & Amendments
body: This policy is reviewed periodically or upon a material change in technical architecture or services, a significant security incident, a change in law, a change in customer requirements, or a change in the risk model.

ZynReach may amend this policy from time to time to reflect technical developments, legal changes, security improvements, lessons learned from incidents, and operational changes; the updated version is published through appropriate channels.

sections.heading: 29. Order of Precedence & Incident Contact
body: In the event of a conflict between this policy and any signed written agreement, the agreement's provisions govern, unless mandatory law provides otherwise; with respect to Customer Data, the Data Processing Agreement is the primary reference regarding the parties' responsibilities, incident notification, deadlines, cooperation, and breach-related obligations.

To report a security incident or suspected data breach to ZynReach, official security or legal contact channels must be used, ideally including the name of the organization or customer, contact details, the nature of the incident, its approximate date and time, the account or service affected, and the data believed to be affected — passwords, API keys, or confidential credentials should never be sent in the report itself.

sections.heading: 30. Legal Notice
body: This document represents the general framework ZynReach uses to manage, respond to, and notify affected parties of security incidents; it does not itself guarantee that ZynReach will detect, prevent, or contain every security incident, nor does it constitute an admission that any particular incident constitutes a legal data breach.

Notification obligations vary by jurisdiction, the nature of the data, ZynReach's role as Controller or Processor, the type of incident, the nature of the risk, the agreement with the customer, and legal and regulatory requirements; the final notification obligation, its content, and its timing are determined according to the law, the agreement, and the facts available in the relevant case. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
body: This Vulnerability Disclosure Policy ("VDP") sets out the procedures and rules ZynReach follows for receiving, verifying, addressing, and communicating about potential security vulnerability reports, aiming to encourage responsible reporting, protect customers and users, reduce security risk, prevent unauthorized exploitation, and provide a clear channel for security researchers to help improve ZynReach's platform security.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of the Policy & Out-of-Scope Assets
body: This policy applies to assets and services owned or operated by ZynReach that are expressly listed within its scope (ZynReach's official website, its official applications, official APIs, and services expressly announced as within testing scope); the appearance of a domain, IP address, or service associated with ZynReach does not automatically mean testing it is authorized.

Unless stated otherwise, the following are considered out of scope: customer systems and accounts, employee systems, third-party services, cloud infrastructure not directly managed by ZynReach, domains not owned or managed by ZynReach, vendor systems, users' personal services, and any system expressly designated in writing as out of scope.

sections.heading: 3. Purpose of Testing & Definition of a Vulnerability
body: Any security testing must be directed solely at discovering and demonstrating a vulnerability without causing unnecessary harm, and may not be used for personal or commercial gain or to obtain data not belonging to the researcher.

A vulnerability means any flaw or weakness in design, implementation, or configuration that could reasonably lead to unauthorized access, privilege escalation, data disclosure or modification, service disruption, execution of unauthorized commands, account compromise, or an effect on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of a system.

sections.heading: 4. Responsible Disclosure & Reporting Channel
body: ZynReach is committed to encouraging responsible disclosure — reporting a vulnerability to ZynReach in a way that allows the Company to verify and address it before details are published that could enable others to exploit it.

Security researchers may report vulnerabilities through the official security channel ZynReach designates on its website; that official channel must be used instead of publicly disclosing vulnerability details.

sections.heading: 5. Report Information & Minimum Evidence
body: A report should ideally include a clear title, a description of the vulnerability, the affected asset, reproduction steps, a safe proof of concept, the expected security impact, a suggested severity level, and any useful technical information — preferably in a structured format: Title (severity and short description), Affected Asset, Description, Steps to Reproduce, Proof of Concept, Impact, Suggested Remediation (optional), and Researcher Contact.
Only the minimum evidence necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability should be provided, without collecting or retaining more personal or confidential data than necessary.

sections.heading: 6. Data Encountered During Testing
body: If testing unintentionally exposes personal data, customer data, credentials, or API keys, the researcher must immediately stop accessing it, not copy, download, use, or share it, and notify ZynReach immediately; researchers are prohibited from attempting to access customer data or personal data not belonging to them, and doing so unnecessarily is considered exceeding the testing scope.

sections.heading: 7. Prohibition on Data Modification & Service Disruption
body: Researchers may not delete, modify, encrypt, transfer, destroy, or alter the permissions of data except to the minimum extent strictly necessary to demonstrate a vulnerability and consistent with this policy.

Any testing that could reasonably lead to denial-of-service, service disruption, resource exhaustion, or system instability is prohibited, and load, stress, or flooding tests may not be performed on production systems without prior written authorization.

sections.heading: 8. Prohibition on Malware & Post-Proof Exploitation
body: Installing malware, ransomware, backdoors, persistence mechanisms, cryptominers, or any tool intended to cause harm or maintain unauthorized access is prohibited.

Once a vulnerability has been demonstrated, the researcher must stop exploiting it; continuing for the purpose of escalating privileges, accessing other systems, extracting additional data, or demonstrating broader scope than necessary is not permitted. Using a ZynReach vulnerability to access customer, vendor, third-party, or other users' systems is also prohibited.

sections.heading: 9. Account Takeover & Authentication/Authorization Testing
body: Where a vulnerability could enable account takeover, the researcher must use a test account they own wherever possible; taking over another user's account or accessing a real account's data is prohibited.

Authentication mechanisms may be tested in a limited and responsible manner, avoiding credential stuffing, large-scale password spraying, or brute force against real accounts; authorization flaws may be tested using appropriate test accounts, without using real users' accounts without authorization.

sections.heading: 10. Automated Scanning & Rate Limits
body: Automated scanning tools may be used if they are rate-limited, non-destructive, do not cause undue load, and are directed at authorized assets; usage limits and request rates must be respected, and ZynReach may block or restrict testing sources that pose a risk to the service.

sections.heading: 11. Out-of-Scope Testing Types
body: This policy generally does not include social engineering (email, phone, or SMS phishing, impersonation, or targeting employees) or physical security testing or facility entry, except with prior express written authorization; ZynReach employees may not be targeted or deceived into providing passwords, authentication codes, or confidential information without prior consent.
Denial-of-service testing is not accepted as part of this policy without prior authorization, and ZynReach's services may not be used to send unsolicited messages or harmful content during testing.

sections.heading: 12. Third-Party & Shared Vulnerabilities
body: If a vulnerability is discovered in a third-party service used by ZynReach, it should be reported to ZynReach where it has a clear effect on ZynReach, and may also be reported to the third party under its own disclosure policy.
Where a vulnerability results from a third-party component, library, or service, ZynReach may need to coordinate with the vendor or responsible party before public disclosure.

sections.heading: 13. Safe Harbor & Good Faith
body: Where a researcher complies in good faith with this policy and does not exceed its scope, ZynReach regards compliant security research activity as responsible and authorized within the limits of this policy; this does not mean granting open authorization to all systems, allowing access to others' data, permitting destructive testing, or granting any rights beyond the scope of the disclosed assets.
Testing must always be conducted in good faith, be non-harmful, limited, and proportionate to the purpose of demonstrating the vulnerability.

sections.heading: 14. Do No Harm & Stopping Tests
body: Researchers must take all reasonable steps to prevent data loss, service disruption, privacy violations, disclosure of confidential information, or impact on customers.
Testing must stop immediately if a system becomes unstable, customer data appears, a risk to the service arises, the asset is discovered to be out of scope, or ZynReach requests that testing stop.

sections.heading: 15. Cleanup & No Data Retention
body: After testing concludes, any files, test accounts, tokens, or test tools or data the researcher created must be removed, to the extent within the researcher's control; any sensitive data unintentionally obtained must not be retained and must be deleted immediately after reporting, unless reasonably necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability and coordinated with ZynReach.

sections.heading: 16. Proof of Concept Standards
body: A proof of concept must be minimal, non-destructive, reproducible, and directly relevant to the vulnerability, and must not include unnecessary confidential data.

sections.heading: 17. Severity Classification & Final Determination
body: ZynReach may classify vulnerabilities as: Critical (may lead to broad system compromise or large-scale disclosure of sensitive data), High (may lead to significant access or impact), Medium (limited security impact or requiring additional conditions to exploit), or Low (low impact or high difficulty of exploitation).

Final severity determination is at ZynReach's discretion, based on impact, exploitability, scope of effect, prerequisites, the nature of the data, and the availability of mitigations; ZynReach is not bound by a severity level proposed by the researcher.

sections.heading: 18. Report Verification & Researcher Communication
body: Upon receiving a report, ZynReach may review it, reproduce it, assess its impact, classify it, prioritize it, and route it to the relevant team, and may contact the researcher to request additional information, reproduction steps, an additional proof of concept, or clarification of impact.

sections.heading: 19. Response Time & Vulnerability Verification
body: ZynReach seeks to review security reports within an appropriate time based on report severity, volume of reports, available resources, and complexity of the issue; no estimated response time constitutes a contractual guarantee. ZynReach may confirm the existence of a vulnerability, its reproducibility, the systems affected, and the scope of its impact.

sections.heading: 20. False Positives & Duplicate Reports
body: If ZynReach cannot reproduce an issue, the report may be classified as not reproducible, informational, or a false positive, with the possibility of re-assessment if new information is provided; where the same vulnerability was previously reported, the report may be classified as a duplicate, with ZynReach retaining discretion over further communication with the researcher.

Security observations that do not represent a direct vulnerability, or reports relating to security best-practice improvements, may also be submitted, and ZynReach evaluates them based on their security value.

sections.heading: 21. Non-Qualifying Reports
body: ZynReach may not consider certain types as disclosable vulnerabilities, including but not limited to:
list: Missing security headers with no actual security impact, or general publicly available information.
Self-XSS with no real exploitation path, or clickjacking on non-sensitive pages.
Non-exploitable configuration issues, unsupported software versions without proof of actual impact, or reports based solely on theoretical scenarios.

sections.heading: 22. Confidentiality & Privacy
body: Researchers must respect the privacy rights of all users, and collecting or disclosing personal data not necessary to demonstrate a vulnerability is prohibited; the confidentiality of customer and user data, security details, vulnerability details, credentials, and internal information must be maintained.

ZynReach treats unpublished vulnerability details as sensitive security information, and uses contact information a researcher provides only for handling the report, in accordance with the Privacy Policy and applicable law.

sections.heading: 23. Public & Coordinated Disclosure
body: Vulnerability details, proof of concept, or customer data may not be published before coordinating with ZynReach; ZynReach prefers coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and may agree with the researcher on a disclosure date, level of detail, a CVE identifier where applicable, and attribution to the researcher.

There is no fixed timeline for publicly disclosing every vulnerability; timing is determined by its nature, severity, prevalence, availability of a fix, and risk to users. Where a researcher is legally obligated to disclose, they must, where possible, notify ZynReach beforehand and coordinate on what information will be published, without publishing any customer data, personal data, credentials, or API keys even if obtained during testing.

sections.heading: 24. Researcher Recognition & Compensation
body: With the researcher's consent, ZynReach may credit their name or alias in a recognition list or security report.

Unless a separate bug bounty program is expressly announced, this policy does not constitute a promise to pay monetary rewards, gifts, or compensation; where ZynReach launches a bug bounty program, its terms will be independent of this policy and will define eligibility, asset scope, rewards, exclusions, and payment terms.

sections.heading: 25. No Employment Relationship, Ownership Rights & Trademark Use
body: Participation in the vulnerability disclosure program does not create an employment relationship, agency, partnership, or legal representation between the researcher and ZynReach, and grants no ownership rights in ZynReach, its source code, customer data, or intellectual property.
The ZynReach or Zyntra Digital name or logos may not be used in commercial or marketing activities without authorization, except for a factual reference to the security report as permitted by law.

sections.heading: 26. Policy Abuse & Extortion
body: ZynReach may take appropriate action where this policy is used for unauthorized access, extorting the Company, obtaining unlawful benefit, disrupting services, or publishing stolen data.

Financial demands or threats to publish in exchange for not disclosing are not part of responsible disclosure, and threatening to publish customer data or trade secrets grants the researcher no additional rights under this policy; ZynReach may take appropriate technical and legal action to protect the platform, users, customers, and data, and cooperate with relevant authorities where required by law.

sections.heading: 27. Safe Harbor Limitations
body: The protection described in this policy does not apply to destructive testing, intentional access to others' data, extortion, data theft, service disruption, publishing confidential information, or exploiting a vulnerability for unlawful gain.

sections.heading: 28. Scope Changes & Emergency Security Actions
body: ZynReach may add or remove assets from the policy's scope, and the currently published version applies to new testing.

ZynReach may take immediate security actions (blocking an IP address, disabling a token, closing an endpoint, suspending a test account) where it considers testing to pose a risk to the service or users, and may require a researcher to stop testing immediately where an asset is out of scope, affects production, poses risk to customers or sensitive data, or exceeds the limits of this policy — a stop request must be respected.

sections.heading: 29. Researcher & ZynReach Responsibilities
body: The researcher is responsible for complying with this policy, using safe tools, protecting credentials, and not exceeding scope or harming systems.

ZynReach commits, within its resources and procedures, to receiving reports, assessing them, investigating them, taking appropriate action, communicating where necessary, and improving security controls — without guaranteeing that every report will be fixed or fixed within a specific timeframe; priority is set based on risk level and impact.

sections.heading: 30. Remediation Process & Security Advisories
body: ZynReach may address a vulnerability through a code fix, configuration change, access-control strengthening, monitoring, a compensating control, or an architectural change, depending on the nature of the issue; it may use compensating controls where a direct fix is not appropriate or requires additional time. After remediation, regression testing may be performed to verify the fix's effectiveness, that the issue does not recur, and that no material side effects have emerged.

ZynReach may publish a security advisory where it considers it useful (a general description, severity level, affected systems, the fix, mitigation steps), and may coordinate with a relevant authority to obtain a CVE identifier where applicable.

sections.heading: 31. General Provisions
body: ZynReach may update this policy as needed due to technical, legal, or security changes, or changes in service scope; the version published on official channels is the governing reference unless a different written agreement exists. This policy is governed by the law applicable to ZynReach and grants no rights inconsistent with mandatory law; ZynReach's failure to enforce any provision in a given case does not waive its right to enforce it in the future, and if any provision becomes invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect to the extent permitted by law.

This policy operates in conjunction with the Security & Trust Policy, Incident Response & Security Breach Notification Policy, Enterprise Security Addendum, Privacy Policy, Data Processing Agreement, Acceptable Use Policy, and Terms of Service, and does not amend or waive any of them unless expressly stated.

sections.heading: 32. Contact & Final Authority
body: Security reports must be directed to the official security contact channel published on zynreach.com; where a vulnerability could lead to broad compromise, disclosure of customer data, complete authentication bypass, or widespread service disruption, it is recommended the report be marked "URGENT / CRITICAL SECURITY" in the subject line.

ZynReach reserves the right to determine the scope of this policy, assess risk, determine severity, determine the remediation approach, and determine disclosure timing, without prejudice to the legal rights of the researcher or any other party.

sections.heading: 33. Legal Notice
body: This policy is intended to govern responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities in ZynReach, and does not grant anyone general authorization to test all ZynReach systems, customer systems, or third-party systems; security research activities must be limited to the disclosed scope and conducted responsibly and non-destructively.

This policy does not grant absolute immunity from legal liability, and does not override any rights or obligations established by law or applicable contracts. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
body: This policy aims to establish a formal framework ensuring ZynReach's ability to maintain critical services and operations, reduce the impact of major outages and incidents, respond to disasters and operational disruptions, restore priority services and systems, protect Customer Data, minimize data loss, support customers during outages, and improve ZynReach's resilience to risk — this policy forms part of ZynReach's governance, security, and business continuity framework.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of the Policy
body: This policy applies to operations, systems, and services within ZynReach's control that are necessary to deliver the services, including the ZynReach platform, the production environment, databases, application services, APIs, authentication services, storage, monitoring, logging, backup systems, supporting infrastructure, critical internal operations, and key third-party dependencies; it does not automatically extend to customer systems or infrastructure exclusively under the control of third parties.

sections.heading: 3. Continuity Objectives
body: ZynReach seeks to achieve the following:
list: Protecting data integrity, reducing service-interruption periods, and identifying priority systems.
Ensuring actionable recovery procedures exist and maintaining appropriate communication channels during crises.
Periodically testing recovery plans, reviewing them after incidents and tests, and continuously improving operational resilience.

sections.heading: 4. BCDR Principles
body: ZynReach relies on the following principles:
list: Resilience: designing processes and systems to reasonably withstand anticipated failures. Recovery: maintaining organized mechanisms for restoring critical services.
Redundancy: using redundancy and alternatives where technically and economically appropriate. Prioritization: giving priority to the most important services and systems.
Continuous Improvement: improving continuity plans based on tests, incidents, and changes in risk.

sections.heading: 5. Definition of a Disaster
body: For the purposes of this policy, a "disaster" may include any event that materially disrupts critical systems or operations, including infrastructure failure, cloud-service outages, database failure, data loss or corruption, cyberattack, ransomware, security incidents, natural disasters, fire, power failure, network failure, major software failure, human error, failure of a key vendor, or other events with a material impact.

sections.heading: 6. Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
body: Business continuity means ZynReach's ability to maintain or restore essential functions and operations within an appropriate timeframe after a disruption occurs, while disaster recovery means the technical and organizational procedures used to restore systems, applications, databases, data, and infrastructure after a disaster or material failure.

sections.heading: 7. Business Impact Analysis & System Classification
body: ZynReach assesses, under its risk-management program, the impact of losing or disrupting critical functions and systems, including the impact of disruption, the importance of the service, dependencies, affected customers, recovery requirements, and financial, operational, and legal impact.

Systems and services may be classified into levels: Critical (whose disruption materially affects the service), High (of significant importance and requiring restoration within an appropriate period), Medium (whose disruption can be tolerated for a limited period), or Low (non-critical, whose restoration can be deferred).

sections.heading: 8. Recovery Prioritization
body: Recovery order is determined by data safety and security first, then critical services, then core customer-facing services, then supporting services, then non-critical systems.

sections.heading: 9. Recovery Time & Point Objectives (RTO/RPO)
body: The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the planned target time for restoring a function or service after a disruption, and does not represent an absolute guarantee of recovery in every incident unless expressly stated in an SLA or commercial agreement; it is set for each critical service based on risk assessment and infrastructure design.

The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the amount of data loss acceptable in time in a recovery scenario, determined by the type of data, the system, backup technology, and service requirements; no specific RPO constitutes a contractual obligation unless expressly agreed. ZynReach may maintain an internal RTO/RPO matrix for each critical system, updated upon material changes.

sections.heading: 10. Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Plans
body: ZynReach maintains appropriate continuity plans for critical operations and services, which may include emergency procedures, responsibilities, contacts, alternatives, recovery priorities, and escalation mechanisms.

It also maintains a disaster recovery plan suited to the nature of its services, which may include activation criteria, recovery procedures, system dependencies, backup recovery, infrastructure and database recovery, validation, and failback.

sections.heading: 11. Disaster Recovery Architecture & External Dependencies
body: Depending on the technical design of the service, ZynReach uses appropriate means to increase infrastructure resilience, such as redundancy, replication, automated recovery, failover, backup infrastructure, and geographic redundancy — using any particular technology does not mean every service component is protected from every type of disaster.

Where ZynReach relies on cloud providers, the continuity of certain components depends on the availability of their services, and ZynReach manages risks within its control. It identifies, to a reasonable extent, critical external dependencies (cloud providers, DNS, payment, email, authentication, monitoring, and communication providers) and seeks to assess key vendor risk and take appropriate measures such as alternatives and contractual protections.

sections.heading: 12. Backups & Their Protection
body: ZynReach uses appropriate backup mechanisms for data and systems that require them (automated, database, incremental, full, and encrypted backups), consistent with the service's technical design, and applies appropriate controls to protect backups from unauthorized access, modification, deletion, or corruption.

Backup retention periods are determined by the nature of the system, operational requirements, risk, legal requirements, and the Data Retention Policy; ZynReach conducts appropriate tests to verify that backups can be restored, without the existence of backups alone guaranteeing that every copy can be restored under all circumstances.

sections.heading: 13. Database Recovery, Data Integrity & Failover/Failback
body: Recovery plans include procedures for restoring critical databases (database restore, replication recovery, integrity and consistency validation); after restoration, appropriate verification is performed to confirm the integrity of data and systems before fully restoring the service.

Where failover mechanisms are available, they may be used to reduce the impact of component failure, automatically or manually depending on the service's design; once the primary environment stabilizes, failback procedures may be carried out after verifying the integrity of systems and data.

sections.heading: 14. Crisis Management & Incident Commander
body: Upon a material incident, ZynReach may activate crisis-management procedures, including forming an incident response team, appointing an incident commander, determining recovery priorities, managing communications, coordinating technical teams, and documenting decisions.

The incident commander coordinates the response, sets priorities, manages escalation, coordinates teams, tracks recovery, and manages internal communications; whether an event requires activating the disaster-recovery plan is determined by the level of impact, duration of disruption, scope of the problem, and recoverability through normal means.

sections.heading: 15. Incident Severity & Escalation
body: Incidents may be classified as: Critical (broad, material impact on a core service), High (significant impact on an important function), Medium (limited impact manageable through normal operations), or Low (minor impact).
Escalation is carried out according to incident severity, and may include technical, management, security, and legal escalation, as well as customer communication.

sections.heading: 16. Communication During Disasters
body: ZynReach maintains appropriate channels for communication during major incidents (email, status page, support channels, internal management channels), and where a material incident affects services provided to a customer, it may provide appropriate updates consistent with the SLA, Terms of Service, DPA, and Incident Response Policy.

ZynReach may use a status page to inform customers of outages, maintenance, known issues, and recovery, and secure communication channels must be used when handling sensitive incident-related information.

sections.heading: 17. Cyber Disaster Recovery & Ransomware Response
body: Recovery plans include security scenarios such as ransomware, malware, account compromise, data corruption, unauthorized access, and infrastructure attacks.

Where ransomware is suspected, ZynReach may isolate affected systems, prevent spread, protect backups, investigate the scope of impact, restore systems from trusted sources, and verify environment integrity before resuming operations — while seeking to use appropriate controls to reduce the likelihood that backups are affected by large-scale security incidents.

sections.heading: 18. Recovery Validation & Post-Recovery Monitoring
body: Before a service is considered restored, appropriate validation tests are performed depending on the nature of the incident (application health checks, database integrity checks, authentication, API, and security tests), and monitoring levels may be increased for an appropriate period after restoration to confirm service stability.

Where a primary communication channel fails, alternative channels defined within internal emergency procedures may be used, and ZynReach maintains, where appropriate, operational capability allowing certain functions to continue from alternate locations or environments.

sections.heading: 19. Essential Personnel & Role Redundancy
body: ZynReach identifies functions and roles considered essential during emergencies (engineering, infrastructure, security, operations, customer support, management, legal), and seeks to reduce reliance on a single individual for critical functions through documented procedures, knowledge sharing, identified backups, and cross-training.

sections.heading: 20. Asset & Recovery Procedure Documentation
body: Appropriate information about systems and assets necessary for recovery is maintained, and critical recovery procedures must be documented in a manner that allows authorized personnel to execute them; recovery procedures are subject to appropriate access controls, and high-risk procedures may only be performed by authorized individuals.

sections.heading: 21. Change Management During Disasters
body: Emergency procedures may be applied to accelerate changes during critical incidents (to stop the spread of an incident, restore service, protect data, or prevent additional harm), with changes required to be documented and reviewed after the crisis ends, and material decisions made during incidents documented (the decision, time, responsible person, rationale, and outcome) where possible.

sections.heading: 22. Testing Program
body: ZynReach conducts appropriate tests of its BCDR plan, including tabletop exercises, backup restore tests, failover tests, recovery simulations, and communication tests; tabletop scenarios may be run to review teams' ability to respond without affecting the production environment, and system/data restoration may be tested periodically based on risk and priority.
Results of significant tests are documented (scenario, date, systems, outcome, issues, corrective actions).

sections.heading: 23. Lessons Learned, Corrective Actions & Policy Review
body: After significant tests or incidents, lessons learned and appropriate corrective actions are identified (action, owner, priority, target date, status), and continuity and recovery plans are reviewed periodically, after major incidents and significant tests, and upon changes in technical architecture, services, or the emergence of new risks — taking into account the effect of material changes on RTO, RPO, dependencies, backups, and availability.

sections.heading: 24. Vendor Risk & Dependency on External Services
body: Where a key vendor fails, ZynReach assesses its impact and activates alternative measures where available; ZynReach does not guarantee the continuity of all external services, so the full recovery of certain functions may depend on the restoration of vendor services.

sections.heading: 25. Data Security During Recovery
body: Appropriate security controls must be maintained during recovery operations, and an emergency must not result in unjustifiably removing security controls; temporary access may be granted during recovery where necessary, subject to restricted scope, logged use, and revocation once no longer needed, and credentials, API keys, encryption keys, and secrets must be protected throughout recovery operations.

Recovery procedures do not automatically change the Data Retention Policy, and deletion is handled consistent with applicable policies, contracts, and laws even during recovery operations, to the extent practicable.

sections.heading: 26. Disaster Recovery Documentation
body: Sufficient documentation must be maintained to support execution of the recovery plan, including architecture diagrams, recovery runbooks, contact lists, system dependencies, backup procedures, and escalation procedures; dedicated runbooks may be created for critical systems including recovery and validation steps, and access to sensitive runbooks is restricted on a least-privilege basis.

sections.heading: 27. Governance & Roles
body: Management may establish a business-continuity committee or team responsible for reviewing risks and plans, tracking tests, and following up on corrective actions, and management is responsible for providing the resources, authority, priorities, and support the BCDR program needs.

The security team's responsibilities may include supporting incident response, assessing security risk, protecting data, and supporting safe recovery; engineering/infrastructure responsibilities include restoring systems, databases, backups, failover, and validation; customer support responsibilities include receiving customer reports, relaying appropriate information, updating customers, and escalating critical issues; and legal/compliance may participate in legal notifications, regulatory requirements, and assessing contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 28. Customer Responsibility & Shared Responsibility
body: The customer remains responsible for its own internal continuity plans, its systems, devices, local data, integrations it manages, and its user accounts; service continuity relies on a shared-responsibility model — ZynReach is responsible for systems within its control, while the customer is responsible for systems and operations within its own control.

Enterprise customers should assess their reliance on ZynReach and prepare appropriate contingency plans for their own business where necessary; ZynReach may provide mechanisms for exporting data consistent with the plan, agreement, and available functionality.

sections.heading: 29. Disclosure to Enterprise Customers
body: Enterprise customers may request appropriate information about ZynReach's BCDR program, subject to confidentiality, security, other customers' rights, and trade secrets, and appropriate summaries or evidence of continuity tests may be provided where the nature of the agreement allows.
ZynReach is not obligated to disclose details of recovery architecture or security architecture whose disclosure could increase security risk.

sections.heading: 30. Relationship to the SLA & Other Documents
body: Where a separate Service Level Agreement exists, any specific contractual commitments regarding availability, RTO, RPO, or service credits are governed by the terms of that SLA; this policy operates in conjunction with the Incident Response & Security Breach Notification Policy, the Security & Trust Policy, the Data Retention & Deletion Policy, and the Data Processing Agreement. Where an Enterprise Security Addendum exists, this policy is read together with it, and where a customer's contract contains a specific BCDR commitment, the commercial agreement governs to the extent of any conflict.

sections.heading: 31. Availability & No-Data-Loss Disclaimers
body: No internal recovery objectives constitute a contractual guarantee unless expressly included in an SLA or commercial agreement; ZynReach works to achieve appropriate levels of resilience and availability, but no guarantee can be made that no outage, failure, or disaster will occur, and backups or recovery procedures do not constitute an absolute guarantee against data loss under all circumstances.

This policy does not affect the force-majeure provisions in the Terms of Service or commercial agreement; where an event involves a security incident, relevant incident-response procedures apply in addition to BCDR procedures, and ZynReach complies with applicable legal and regulatory requirements relating to business continuity and data protection.

sections.heading: 32. Confidentiality, Exceptions & Violations
body: Sensitive BCDR information (recovery architecture, runbooks, security details) is treated as confidential and is not published publicly except to an appropriate extent, and records relating to tests, incidents, and corrective actions are retained per internal retention policies.

Any material exception to this policy must be documented, justified, approved by the relevant authority, and time-limited where possible; violations of this policy's requirements may result in corrective action, management review, changes to permissions, or disciplinary action per internal policies.

sections.heading: 33. Continuous Improvement & Periodic Review
body: ZynReach is committed to continuously reviewing and improving its BCDR program based on incidents, tests, technical changes, new risks, customer requirements, and legal requirements, and this policy is reviewed periodically per ZynReach's internal review cycle, or upon a material change requiring it.

sections.heading: 34. Legal Notice
body: This document represents a general framework for ZynReach's business continuity and disaster recovery program, and, unless expressly incorporated into a commercial agreement, does not constitute a contractual guarantee of a specific level of availability, RTO, RPO, or freedom from data loss; obligations specific to each Enterprise customer are governed by applicable agreements, contracts, SLAs, and the DPA. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
body: This Enterprise Security Addendum ("ESA") sets out the security requirements and obligations applicable to ZynReach services provided to Enterprise customers, and aims to explain ZynReach's security framework, technical and organizational measures, access management, data protection, encryption, infrastructure security, vulnerability and incident management, business continuity, backup and disaster recovery, management of third parties and sub-processors, customer security requirements, incident cooperation, and audit and compliance evidence.

This addendum forms part of the commercial agreement between ZynReach and the customer where it is incorporated or expressly referenced in an order form, a Master Services Agreement, or a similar agreement.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of Application
body: This addendum applies to the ZynReach services specified in the agreement or order form, and does not automatically extend to third-party services not controlled by ZynReach, customer systems, user devices, customer networks, integrations managed by the customer, or external applications, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

sections.heading: 3. Definitions
list: Security Incident: a confirmed or reasonably suspected security event resulting, or that could result, in unauthorized access, unauthorized loss or alteration of data, unauthorized disclosure, or material service disruption.
Personal Data: personal data as defined under applicable law. Customer Data: data provided by the customer or its users to ZynReach, or generated on the customer's behalf through use of the services.

Sub-processor: a third party that processes Customer Data on ZynReach's behalf under the relevant contractual relationship. Security Controls: the technical, organizational, and administrative controls ZynReach uses to protect the services.

sections.heading: 4. Security Framework & Information Security Management Program
body: ZynReach is committed to maintaining a security program appropriate to the nature of the services and their associated risks, aimed at protecting confidentiality, integrity, availability, and operational resilience, without this meaning that ZynReach guarantees the services will be immune to all threats or security incidents.

ZynReach seeks to operate a structured information-security management program that includes, depending on the nature and scale of the services, security policies, risk assessments, asset management, access management, vulnerability management, security monitoring, incident management, business continuity, vendor management, and training and awareness.

sections.heading: 5. Management Responsibility & Risk Assessment
body: ZynReach maintains clear management responsibility for its security program, defining responsibilities, authorities, escalation procedures, operational risk ownership, and review mechanisms.

ZynReach assesses security risks periodically or upon material changes to services, infrastructure, threats, operations, or legal requirements, and may use the results of risk assessments to prioritize security controls.

sections.heading: 6. Policy Management, Personnel Security & Training
body: ZynReach maintains appropriate security policies and procedures for its services, reviewed periodically and upon material changes, and applies appropriate measures to manage the security of personnel with access to sensitive systems (appropriate pre-employment screening where permitted by law, confidentiality agreements, security training, defined permissions, access-termination procedures).

ZynReach provides appropriate security awareness for personnel whose roles require it, covering topics such as credential protection, phishing, data protection, incident management, device security, and social engineering.

sections.heading: 7. Access Management, Role-Based Access Control & Multi-Factor Authentication
body: ZynReach applies the principle of least privilege, granting access only to the extent necessary to perform tasks, and uses appropriate controls to manage access by job role, restricting access to systems and data based on need.
ZynReach uses multi-factor authentication for systems and accounts requiring a heightened level of protection, based on risk and the service's technical design.

sections.heading: 8. Permission Review, Access Termination & Administrative Accounts
body: Access permissions to sensitive systems are reviewed periodically or upon material changes in functions or responsibilities, and when an employee's or contractor's need for access ends, access is revoked or modified per ZynReach's internal procedures.

Accounts with elevated privileges are subject to additional appropriate controls, which may include multi-factor authentication, privileged access controls, logging, access review, and segregation of duties.

sections.heading: 9. Credential Protection & Encryption
body: ZynReach applies appropriate measures to protect passwords, API keys, tokens, secrets, and encryption keys, and storing sensitive credentials in an inappropriate manner is prohibited.

ZynReach uses appropriate encryption to protect data in transit over public networks and at rest, consistent with the service's technical design and the nature of the data, and encryption keys are managed under appropriate procedures to protect their confidentiality, access, lifecycle, and against unauthorized use.

sections.heading: 10. Customer Data Isolation & Isolation Testing
body: ZynReach uses appropriate technical controls to separate customer data and environments consistent with the platform's design; no customer may access another customer's data through normal use of the service. ZynReach may use appropriate technical tests to verify isolation controls, depending on the service's design and risk.

sections.heading: 11. Secure Software Development & Application Security
body: ZynReach integrates appropriate security practices into the software development lifecycle (secure coding, code review, dependency management, security testing, vulnerability management, change management), and seeks to build security requirements into the design, development, testing, deployment, and operation stages.

Significant code changes undergo appropriate review commensurate with risk level, and ZynReach works to identify and manage software components and dependencies used in the services, scanning them for known vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: 12. Vulnerability Management, Security Testing & Responsible Disclosure
body: ZynReach applies an appropriate process for discovering vulnerabilities, assessing risk, prioritizing, remediating, and verifying fixes; vulnerabilities may be classified by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low), with remediation timeframes varying by severity, complexity, and impact.

ZynReach may conduct appropriate security tests (vulnerability scanning, security testing, penetration testing, application security testing) consistent with the nature of the service and its risks, and provides, where appropriate, a mechanism for responsible reporting of security vulnerabilities that researchers must comply with in terms of scope and rules.

sections.heading: 13. Logging & Monitoring
body: ZynReach maintains appropriate security and operational logs to support incident detection, investigation, troubleshooting, audit, and monitoring, and uses appropriate monitoring means to detect abnormal activity, unauthorized access attempts, security threats, performance issues, and outages, while applying appropriate controls to protect logs from unauthorized modification, deletion, or access.

sections.heading: 14. Incident Management & Notification
body: ZynReach maintains a security-incident management program that includes detection, initial triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.

Upon confirming a security incident affecting Customer Data, ZynReach notifies the customer per the DPA, the agreement, and applicable law, using reasonably available information to provide a useful notification that includes, depending on the information available, a general description of the incident, its date, the nature of the impact, affected categories, measures taken, remedial measures, and appropriate contact information, without any requirement to include unconfirmed information that could hinder the investigation or increase security risk.

sections.heading: 15. Incident Cooperation & Communication
body: ZynReach cooperates reasonably with the customer in investigations relating to a security incident affecting its data, within the limits of the agreement, the DPA, applicable law, and security constraints, and defines appropriate channels for escalation and communication about security incidents, which may vary by customer tier and service.

sections.heading: 16. Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
body: ZynReach maintains appropriate procedures to support the continuity of critical services and operations, and maintains disaster-recovery plans suited to the nature of its services (system and data recovery, failover, recovery procedures), conducting appropriate tests or exercises to verify the effectiveness of recovery procedures per its internal practices.
ZynReach uses appropriate backup mechanisms for services that require them, with controls including backup encryption, access control, monitoring, and restoration testing.

sections.heading: 17. Change Management
body: Material changes to infrastructure and services undergo appropriate change-management processes, which may include impact assessment, review, testing, approval, documentation, and a rollback plan.

sections.heading: 18. Infrastructure, Cloud, Network & Endpoint Security
body: Where ZynReach relies on cloud or data-center providers, it relies on the security controls those providers offer in addition to controls within ZynReach's own responsibility; ZynReach's responsibility does not extend to controls exclusively under the infrastructure provider's control, and cloud vendors and their associated controls are assessed under applicable procedures.

Depending on technical architecture, ZynReach uses controls such as firewalls, network segmentation, access controls, and traffic monitoring, applies appropriate measures to protect devices used to access enterprise systems (security updates, device encryption, malware protection, appropriate monitoring), and relies on the physical and security controls provided by cloud and data-center providers.

sections.heading: 19. Vendor & Sub-processor Security
body: ZynReach applies appropriate measures to assess the security risk of vendors that may have access to systems, data, or infrastructure, and may use sub-processors per the DPA and Sub-processor Policy, remaining contractually responsible to the customer for its processing obligations to the extent set out in the DPA; ZynReach may add or replace sub-processors per the notification and objection mechanism set out in the DPA.

sections.heading: 20. Data Retention, Deletion & Minimization
body: ZynReach retains data per applicable retention policies and agreements, and after the service ends, Customer Data is processed per the DPA, Terms of Service, Data Retention & Deletion Policy, and legal requirements.

ZynReach seeks to consider privacy and security during the design and development of its services (privacy by design) and to minimize the collection and processing of data to what is appropriate for delivering the services.

sections.heading: 21. Customer Security Responsibilities & Shared Responsibility Model
body: The customer acknowledges that service security is a shared responsibility, and remains responsible for its accounts, users, passwords, multi-factor authentication, devices, networks under its control, integrations, permission settings, and the data it chooses to enter into the service; ZynReach's security measures do not exempt the customer from its own security responsibilities.
The customer must create accounts for authorized users, deactivate unneeded accounts, review permissions, protect login credentials, and prevent unauthorized account sharing.

sections.heading: 22. API Security & Third-Party Integrations
body: When using APIs, the customer is responsible for protecting API keys and secrets, applying appropriate permissions, monitoring API usage, and respecting rate limits; ZynReach is not responsible for security risks arising exclusively from misconfigured integrations, customer systems, third-party accounts, or services outside ZynReach's control.

sections.heading: 23. Security Documentation & Independent Audit Reports
body: Enterprise customers may request reasonable information about ZynReach's security controls consistent with the plan, agreement, and confidentiality rights, and ZynReach may provide, depending on the nature of the relationship, a security questionnaire, security overview, policy documents, certificates, audit reports, and compliance evidence, to the extent permitted by confidentiality and commercial security.

Where ZynReach holds current independent audit reports or certifications, they may be provided to the customer subject to applicable restrictions, and providing any report or certificate should not be interpreted as a guarantee that the customer will be compliant with all of its own legal requirements.

sections.heading: 24. Customer Audit Rights & Alternatives
body: The customer may not conduct a direct on-site audit of ZynReach's systems without prior written consent, unless mandatory law grants this right; any audit must be reasonable, defined in scope, related to the services, must not affect the security or stability of the service, and must not disclose unnecessary trade secrets.

ZynReach may satisfy audit requests through independent reports, questionnaires, security documentation, certificates, written answers, or summaries of independent assessments; the customer bears the costs of its own audit unless otherwise agreed, and must maintain the confidentiality of all information obtained during any assessment; an audit may not disrupt the service, disclose other customers' data, or weaken security controls.

sections.heading: 25. Customer-Conducted Testing & Vulnerability Reporting
body: The customer may not conduct penetration testing or security scanning on ZynReach's systems without prior written authorization; where the customer discovers a potential vulnerability, it must be reported through ZynReach's designated security channel rather than exploited or publicly disclosed before coordination.

sections.heading: 26. Record Management, Access Monitoring & No Absolute Security Guarantee
body: ZynReach retains security and operational logs for the period it considers appropriate under legal requirements, security needs, internal policies, and service design, and access to sensitive systems may be logged and monitored for security, investigation, audit, and compliance purposes.

The parties acknowledge that no technical system can be guaranteed protected from all risks, and no statement in this addendum constitutes a guarantee that no breach will occur, that no vulnerability exists, that the service will be 100% available, or that no data will be lost under all circumstances.

sections.heading: 27. Compliance & Relationship to Other Documents
body: ZynReach seeks to manage its services consistent with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and the customer remains responsible for the regulatory requirements specific to its own activity; where ZynReach is a processor of personal data, this addendum is read together with the DPA, and in case of conflict regarding the processing of personal data, the DPA's provisions govern.

General rights relating to use of the services are governed by the Terms of Service, and the customer and its users must comply with the Acceptable Use Policy; ZynReach may take action against use that poses a security risk. Management of sub-processors is governed by the Sub-processor Policy and the DPA, as applicable.

sections.heading: 28. Security Contact & Handling of Incident Information
body: ZynReach maintains an appropriate channel for receiving security reports, and the customer must use the channels specified in the agreement, the trust center, or the official website; neither party is obligated to disclose confidential or sensitive information beyond what is reasonably necessary to handle an incident, and certain information may be delayed or restricted where immediate disclosure would harm the investigation, increase risk, or violate the law, with appropriate information provided once possible.

ZynReach may cooperate with competent legal or regulatory authorities where legally required; where it receives a lawful request for access to customer data, it is handled per applicable law, the DPA, and the agreement.

sections.heading: 29. Data Location, Security Changes & Exceptions
body: Data processing or storage location is determined per the plan, agreement, or available data-residency options, and no specific storage location should be assumed unless expressly stated.

ZynReach may modify security controls where necessary to address a new threat, improve security, update technology, or comply with law; ordinary operational security changes are not considered a breach of the agreement merely because they change how a control is implemented, and urgent security updates may be made without prior notice where necessary. ZynReach may use temporary exceptions from certain operational procedures for technical or security reasons, and may accept certain residual risks where the cost of remediation is disproportionate to the risk level, per its internal risk-management framework.

sections.heading: 30. Recovery Objectives, Addendum Review & Amendments
body: Where specific objectives such as RTO or RPO exist, they must be expressly set out in an SLA or commercial agreement; no values not contractually specified constitute a guaranteed commitment.

This addendum is reviewed periodically or upon a material change in services, a significant legal change, a material change in the threat model, or a significant incident; no amendment to this addendum takes effect as a contractual obligation on the customer except per the amendment mechanism set out in the agreement.

sections.heading: 31. Precedence, Liability, Confidentiality & Additional Addenda
