body: In the event of conflict, the following order applies: mandatory law, then the signed commercial agreement, then the DPA with respect to personal data, then the SLA with respect to service levels, then this addendum, then general policies — applied only to the matter in conflict. This addendum does not, by itself, increase or change the liability limits set out in the commercial agreement unless the agreement expressly states so, and no reference in it to a security practice or control constitutes an independent guarantee beyond express contractual obligations.

All non-public security information provided to the customer under this addendum is confidential, unless lawfully publicly available or the contract states otherwise; the customer may not publish or share penetration-test results, vulnerability reports, system architecture, keys or technical secrets, or incident information except under authorization or legal obligation. The parties may agree on additional addenda, such as a security requirements schedule, a data residency addendum, an incident notification schedule, a business continuity schedule, or customer-specific security controls.

sections.heading: 32. Shared Responsibility, General Provisions & Legal Notice
body: The parties acknowledge that security in a SaaS environment relies on a shared-responsibility model: ZynReach is responsible for controls within its own control, while the customer is responsible for controls, systems, and data within its own control; certain Enterprise agreements may include additional security requirements, which are not binding on ZynReach unless agreed in writing with defined scope, implementation responsibility, and any additional fees or resources — no security questionnaire or sales presentation should be interpreted as amending this agreement unless agreed in writing by authorized representatives.

A party's failure to enforce any provision of this addendum does not constitute a waiver of it, and if any provision becomes invalid, the remaining provisions remain unaffected; this addendum is governed by the governing law specified in the commercial agreement, and disputes relating to it are subject to the dispute-resolution mechanism set out there. This addendum, together with the agreements it references, represents the complete understanding between the parties regarding the security requirements set out in it, and no provision should be interpreted as an absolute guarantee of security, availability, or freedom from incidents. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

data-transfer.title: Data Transfer & International Data Transfer Policy

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
body: This policy explains how ZynReach handles data transfers and processing that may occur across borders or between different countries or geographic regions, and aims to set out the principles of international transfer, protect Customer Data and personal data during transfer, identify the appropriate legal bases for it, govern the use of service providers and third parties, support compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and clarify ZynReach's and customers' responsibilities in this regard.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of the Policy
body: This policy applies to data ZynReach processes in the context of the website, the SaaS platform, APIs, customer support, account management, cloud infrastructure, third-party services, sub-processors, and business operations, and does not apply to data outside ZynReach's control.

sections.heading: 3. Definition of Data & Data Transfer
body: For the purposes of this policy, "data" may include personal data, Customer Data, account data, business data, usage data, technical data, support data, and security logs, each handled according to its nature and applicable legal and contractual obligations.

"Data Transfer" means any operation by which data is transferred, made available, remotely accessed, stored, or processed in a country or region different from the one where it was collected, stored, or processed; "International Data Transfer" means any transfer or availability of personal data across international borders that subjects it to a different legal regime.

sections.heading: 4. Data Transfer Principles
body: ZynReach relies on the principles of lawfulness, transparency, data minimization, purpose limitation, data protection, security, accountability, and respect for individuals' legal rights in its data-transfer operations.

sections.heading: 5. No Guarantee of a Fixed Data Location
body: Unless otherwise contractually agreed, ZynReach does not guarantee that all data associated with a customer's account is stored or processed exclusively within a single country; data may be processed at different locations depending on infrastructure, cloud providers, sub-processors, operational requirements, business continuity, and security.

sections.heading: 6. Data Residency & Regional Hosting
body: Where ZynReach offers a data-residency or regional-hosting option for a particular product or plan, the scope of that option is governed by the Terms of Service, the commercial agreement, and published technical specifications; the mere existence of a data center in a given country does not guarantee that all processing will occur exclusively within that country.

The applicable commercial agreement determines the region, data scope, exceptions, sub-processors, support operations, and backups associated with any regional-hosting option; data may be processed in the customer's country, the country where the infrastructure is located, a sub-processor's country, or a country where a support or operational team is located, depending on the nature of the service.

sections.heading: 7. Lawful Basis for Transfer
body: Where data-protection laws requiring a lawful basis for data transfer apply, ZynReach works to use the appropriate basis depending on the nature of the processing and the location of the parties — whether contractual necessity to perform the agreement or provide the requested service, an applicable legal obligation, a legitimate interest balanced against relevant rights, or express consent where required by law.

sections.heading: 8. Standard Contractual Clauses & Transfer Impact Assessment
body: Where GDPR or similar regimes' requirements apply, ZynReach may rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or another legally recognized contractual mechanism for international data transfer, with the appropriate version or module determined by the nature of the parties and the processing.

Where required or appropriate, ZynReach may conduct a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) to assess the risks of international transfer, which may include the receiving country, its legal system, the nature of the data, the purpose of the transfer, the possibility of government access, security measures, and additional safeguards.

sections.heading: 9. Supplementary Measures & Encryption
body: Where appropriate, additional measures may be applied to protect data during international transfer, such as encryption, access controls, authentication, pseudonymization, data minimization, logging, and monitoring.

ZynReach uses appropriate encryption, where technically appropriate, to protect data while it travels across networks, and stored data may be encrypted consistent with the infrastructure and service design.

sections.heading: 10. Access Control, Authentication, Logging & Monitoring
body: Access to internationally transferred data is restricted on a least-privilege basis, by role and need for access; ZynReach uses appropriate authentication mechanisms to protect systems through which data can be accessed, and access or data-related activities may be logged consistent with security, operational, and legal requirements, with appropriate monitoring used to detect abnormal or unauthorized activity.

sections.heading: 11. Sub-processors & International Transfer
body: ZynReach may rely on sub-processors to process data, and these relationships are governed by the Sub-processor Policy and applicable contractual agreements; some may be located outside the customer's country, which may result in the transfer or availability of data across borders.

ZynReach seeks to assess service providers that may handle data consistent with the nature of the service, the type of data, the risks, and the level of access, and includes appropriate obligations for them regarding confidentiality, security, data protection, data use, incident notification, and data deletion where applicable. ZynReach may publish or make available a sub-processor list per the mechanism set out in the Sub-processor Policy or the DPA, and add or replace sub-processors per the notification and objection procedures set out there; where the customer is granted a right to object to a new sub-processor, it is exercised per the timeframe and procedures specified in the agreement.

sections.heading: 12. Government Requests & Legal Review
body: ZynReach may receive lawful requests from government or judicial authorities for data, and responds only per applicable legal requirements; where permitted by law, it may review a request's validity, scope, the authority's jurisdiction, and its legal basis, and seeks to limit disclosed data to what is legally required.

Where the law permits, ZynReach may notify the customer of a government request relating to its data; this is not possible where the law prohibits it. Disclosure may occur in emergencies where permitted or required by law, and where a foreign law-enforcement authority requests data, ZynReach assesses the request under applicable law and relevant legal agreements.

sections.heading: 13. Intra-Group Transfers & Internal Cross-Border Access
body: Data may be shared or transferred between ZynReach's group companies or affiliates where necessary to provide the services or operate the business, consistent with law and agreements.

Certain ZynReach employees, support teams, or security teams may have remote access to data from a different country, subject to authorization, access control, security policies, confidentiality, and monitoring; providing technical or security support may require limited access to account information, subject to appropriate permissions, business need, the customer agreement, and data-protection policies. Remote access to data from another country is considered a form of data transfer where applicable law applies to it.

sections.heading: 14. Customer Data Export & Customer-Initiated Transfers
body: The customer may export its data per the platform's functionality and its agreement, and is responsible for handling the data after exporting it to its own systems.

Where the customer chooses to integrate a third-party service, export data, share data, or connect an external platform, this may result in data being transferred to other countries, and the customer is responsible for ensuring the legality of these operations within its own control. When enabling an external integration, data may pass to the third party per the integration's settings, and the customer must review that third party's own privacy policy and terms. Data may also be transferred via APIs between ZynReach and the customer's systems or external systems, subject to appropriate authentication and security controls.

sections.heading: 15. Data Protection in Transit & At Rest
body: ZynReach applies appropriate controls to protect data while it moves between systems and while it is stored, consistent with the service's architecture.

sections.heading: 16. Backup & Disaster Recovery Transfers
body: Data may be backed up or replicated to other locations for disaster recovery, business continuity, and availability purposes, which may involve transferring data between different geographic regions; disaster-recovery operations may involve using infrastructure or backups located in a different geographic region, subject to appropriate security and privacy controls. ZynReach may use replication between different environments or regions to support availability, resilience, and disaster recovery.

sections.heading: 17. Sensitive Data & Special Categories
body: Where the service permits processing sensitive data or special categories of data, additional requirements may apply to its transfer, and the customer must not enter such data unless permitted under the service and agreement; where GDPR applies, ZynReach handles special categories of personal data per relevant legal requirements.

sections.heading: 18. Customer Responsibility & Controller/Processor Roles
body: The customer remains responsible for determining the data it enters into the platform, the legal basis for processing, ensuring the legality of transferring the data, and fulfilling its own obligations under data-protection laws.

The parties' roles vary by the nature of the processing, and ZynReach may act as a Data Processor, a service provider, or a Data Controller for certain of its own operational data; the DPA and Privacy Policy determine the applicable role.

sections.heading: 19. Data Processing Agreement & Its Priority
body: Where ZynReach acts as a Processor for the customer, data-processing and transfer operations are governed by the Data Processing Agreement (DPA) between the parties; in the event of a conflict between this policy and an effective DPA, the DPA's provisions govern to the extent necessary to resolve the conflict.

sections.heading: 20. Applicable Data Protection Laws
body: Where GDPR applies to a given processing activity, ZynReach seeks to comply with its international-transfer requirements to the extent applicable, and where UK GDPR applies, it may rely on transfer mechanisms recognized under UK law.

Transfer operations may be subject to other laws, such as local or regional data-protection laws or cross-border data-transfer laws, and ZynReach determines the appropriate mechanism based on the scope of applicable law; it may assess international-transfer requirements where necessary due to the customer's country, the nature of the data, the place of processing, a sub-processor, or applicable law.

sections.heading: 21. Transfer Mechanisms
body: One of the available lawful transfer mechanisms may be used, as applicable: an adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses, an approved contractual mechanism, Binding Corporate Rules, consent, a statutory exception, or another mechanism permitted by law.

Where a competent regulatory authority recognizes that a country or region provides an adequate level of protection, an adequacy decision may be relied upon to the extent permitted; where SCCs are the appropriate mechanism, they are incorporated into relevant agreements per legal requirements, with supplementary security measures applied where needed.

sections.heading: 22. Transfer Risk & Risk-Based Approach
body: ZynReach recognizes that international transfer may involve additional risks, including differing data-protection laws, government authority requests, unauthorized-access risk, and vendor risk, and handles them using a risk-based approach.

ZynReach seeks to limit data transfer to what is necessary to achieve the specified purpose, and transferred data should not be used for purposes incompatible with the purpose for which it was collected or processed.

sections.heading: 23. Retention & Deletion of Transferred Data
body: Transferred data remains subject to the Data Retention & Deletion Policy and applicable agreements; once the need for the data or the retention period ends, it is deleted or destroyed per applicable policies and contracts. Deletion may require removing data from production systems, backups, replicas, and disaster-recovery environments per applicable technical retention schedules, acknowledging that some data may persist in backups for a limited time after deletion from production due to the nature of backup systems.

sections.heading: 24. Security Incidents & Breach Notification
body: Where a security incident affects international data-transfer operations, the Incident Response & Security Breach Notification Policy applies; where an incident gives rise to a legal notification obligation, ZynReach takes the required actions per applicable law and agreements, and certain incidents may require coordination between teams or entities located in different countries.

sections.heading: 25. Documentation & Records of Processing
body: ZynReach retains, where applicable, records relating to international transfer operations and related safeguards, and where legal requirements apply, may maintain appropriate processing records including information relating to data-transfer operations.

sections.heading: 26. Audits & Transparency
body: Qualified customers may request reasonable information or evidence about international data-protection mechanisms under the DPA; audits are subject to confidentiality, security, protection of other customers, non-disruption of services, and reasonable costs where applicable. Where relevant independent audit reports or certifications are available, ZynReach may provide them subject to applicable access terms.
ZynReach seeks to provide appropriate information about processing locations, sub-processors, and transfer mechanisms, to the extent permitted by security, confidentiality, and contracts.

sections.heading: 27. Infrastructure Changes & Customer Notice
body: Changes to cloud architecture, sub-processors, data centers, or disaster-recovery systems may result in changes to data-processing locations, and these changes are managed per appropriate change procedures.

Where notice is contractually required, customers are notified per the terms of the agreement; where the agreement or DPA grants the customer a right to object to a change affecting international transfer, the objection is handled per the procedures set out in the agreement.

sections.heading: 28. International Employee Access to Data
body: Certain authorized employees or contractors may be able to access data from outside the customer's country, subject to access control, confidentiality, authentication, monitoring, and security training, with access to international data granted only to the extent necessary to perform the function (least privilege).

Individuals with access to the data must maintain its confidentiality per applicable contracts and policies, and ZynReach applies appropriate measures to manage its employees' and contractors' access to systems and data, protecting encryption keys per its approved security controls; data-transfer operations must occur through channels and systems appropriate for security protection, and any unauthorized data transfer discovered is treated as a security incident where applicable.

sections.heading: 29. Customer Configuration & International Customers
body: Certain products may allow customers to control integrations, data exports, user access, and regional settings, and the customer is responsible for using these options lawfully and securely; international customers may use ZynReach per the regions and services available to them, subject to relevant legal and technical restrictions.

sections.heading: 30. Restricted Jurisdictions & Sanctions/Export Controls
body: ZynReach may restrict or prohibit certain services in specific countries or regions where legally required, necessary for compliance, or required for security reasons; certain services or technologies may be subject to sanctions laws or export controls, and ZynReach may take appropriate action to comply with applicable laws.
ZynReach may not be used to circumvent sanctions laws, export restrictions, data-protection requirements, or legal geographic restrictions.

sections.heading: 31. Policy Changes, Relationship to Other Documents & Order of Precedence
body: ZynReach may update this policy due to legal, regulatory, or technical changes, changes in sub-processors, or changes in its business model; the version currently published on ZynReach's official channels is the effective version unless the customer's agreement states otherwise.

This policy operates in conjunction with the Privacy Policy, Data Processing Agreement, Sub-processor Policy, Data Retention & Deletion Policy, Security & Trust Policy, Enterprise Security Addendum, Incident Response & Security Breach Notification Policy, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Policy, and Terms of Service. In the event of conflict, the following order applies: mandatory applicable law, then the signed commercial agreement, then the DPA, then the SLA/Enterprise Addendum depending on the subject of the conflict, then this policy, then other general policies — this order should not be interpreted as a waiver of any legal right.

sections.heading: 32. Disclaimers, Compliance & Contact
body: This policy does not constitute legal advice to the customer, and each customer is responsible for assessing the requirements of data-protection laws applicable to its own activity and to the data it processes through ZynReach. ZynReach does not guarantee that no international transfer will occur or that data will never reach another country under all circumstances, unless there is an express contractual commitment to that effect; no reference to a hosting region or country constitutes a guarantee that every copy, processing operation, access, or backup will remain exclusively within that region unless the agreement or product expressly states so.

ZynReach seeks to manage international data-transfer operations consistent with the laws and regulations applicable to its activity and the processing concerned; if any provision of this policy becomes invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect to the maximum extent permitted by law, and ZynReach's failure to apply any provision in a given case does not constitute a waiver of its right to apply it later. For inquiries relating to data protection and international data transfer, contact the official privacy and legal email address published on zynreach.com. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
body: This Sub-processor Policy ("Policy") explains how ZynReach, owned and operated by Zyntra Digital ("ZynReach," "the Company," "we," or "us"), selects, assesses, manages, and monitors third parties that may process personal data on behalf of ZynReach or on behalf of its customers.

This Policy is part of ZynReach's privacy, security, and compliance framework and should be read together with the Privacy Policy, the Data Processing Agreement (DPA), the Security & Trust Policy, the Terms of Service / Master Services Agreement, and any privacy or data-security agreements or addenda applicable to the relevant customer. In the event of a conflict between this Policy and any written, signed agreement between ZynReach and a customer, the signed agreement governs to the extent required by law.

sections.heading: 2. Definitions
body: "Customer Data" means data the customer provides to ZynReach or that the customer or its users enter, upload, store, or process through the services. "Personal Data" means any data considered personal data or personal information under applicable law. "Processing" means any operation or set of operations performed on personal data, including collection, storage, use, access, transfer, disclosure, modification, or deletion.

"Processor" means the party that processes personal data on behalf of a Controller or another party legally authorized to do so. "Sub-processor" means any third party engaged by ZynReach to process personal data on behalf of ZynReach or its customers, where that processing relates to the services provided to the customer. "Controller" means the party that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data under applicable law. "Applicable Data Protection Law" means all data-protection and privacy laws and regulations applicable to the relevant processing, depending on the nature of the data, the location of the parties and individuals, and the place of processing.

sections.heading: 3. Scope of the Policy
body: This Policy applies to sub-processors engaged by ZynReach in delivering its services where that third party has access to personal data processed on the customer's behalf; the mere use by ZynReach of an external vendor or service provider does not necessarily make it a Sub-processor.
list: Hosting and cloud infrastructure, data storage, and databases.
Email and messaging services, and technical support services.
Monitoring and logging services, and cybersecurity.
Backup and disaster recovery, analytics services, and communications services.
Artificial intelligence or machine learning services.
Payment-processing services, where personal-data processing is part of the service.
Other technical or operational services necessary to deliver the services.

sections.heading: 4. Core Principle
body: ZynReach commits to engaging a Sub-processor to process personal data only when necessary or appropriate to deliver the services, operate infrastructure, maintain its security, or improve its reliability, and consistent with applicable contractual and legal obligations. ZynReach remains responsible for Sub-processors' actions to the extent required by applicable laws and relevant agreements.

sections.heading: 5. Selection of Sub-processors
body: ZynReach follows appropriate procedures before engaging a new Sub-processor where the nature of the service requires processing personal data on the customer's behalf. ZynReach is not obligated to apply the same level of scrutiny to every Sub-processor; the level of due diligence may be proportionate to the nature of the service and the volume, type, and risk of the data involved.
list: Identifying the nature of the service, the purpose of processing, the types of data involved, and the categories of affected data subjects.
Assessing security and privacy risks and reviewing available technical and organizational controls.
Reviewing the provider's privacy and security policies and assessing where data is stored and processed.
Assessing international data-transfer mechanisms where relevant, and reviewing contractual confidentiality and data-protection obligations.
Assessing security-incident management procedures and data deletion and retention procedures.
Assessing relevant security certifications or accreditations, and conducting additional risk assessment where the processing is highly sensitive or high-risk.

sections.heading: 6. Contractual Requirements
body: ZynReach seeks to impose appropriate contractual obligations on Sub-processors that process personal data on its behalf. A Sub-processor may not use Customer Data for its own purposes except where contractually authorized, legally required, or within an independent, lawful scope that does not constitute processing on ZynReach's behalf.
list: Confidentiality obligations, and processing data per authorized instructions.
Applying appropriate security measures, and restricting access to data.
Reporting security incidents, and cooperating with responses to data-subject requests.
Cooperating on data-protection obligations, and assisting with incident investigations.
Complying with restrictions on international transfer.
Returning or deleting data upon termination of service, and not using data for unauthorized independent purposes.

sections.heading: 7. Sub-processor List
body: ZynReach may publish or make available a list of Sub-processors used in delivering the services through its website, Trust Center, or another appropriate electronic means, which may include the Sub-processor's name, service type, nature of processing, and processing/hosting location — for example, infrastructure and hosting providers (Storage & Processing), communications providers (Email/Messaging), security-monitoring providers (Security Monitoring), and support-services providers (Customer Support).

This list does not itself constitute a commitment to use any specific vendor for the duration of the contractual relationship, and ZynReach may change or replace Sub-processors per the provisions of this Policy and applicable agreements.

sections.heading: 8. Adding or Replacing Sub-processors
body: ZynReach may add or replace a Sub-processor where necessary or appropriate for operational, technical, security, or business reasons, including improving security, performance, or reliability; providing more efficient infrastructure; developing the services; replacing an existing vendor; business continuity; legal or regulatory requirements; reducing risk; or introducing new functionality or services. Where required under the DPA or applicable law, ZynReach notifies the customer before engaging a new Sub-processor per the mechanism and timeframe specified in the applicable agreement.

sections.heading: 9. Notification of Changes
body: Customers may be notified of changes relating to Sub-processors through one or more of the following: updating the published Sub-processor list; sending an email notice; an in-platform notice; a notice through the customer portal; updating the Trust Center; or any other means permitted by the applicable agreement. Where the customer's agreement specifies a different notification mechanism, the contractually agreed mechanism applies.

sections.heading: 10. Right to Object
body: Where the DPA or applicable law grants the customer a right to object to the engagement of a new Sub-processor, the customer may submit a written objection within the period specified in the DPA or relevant agreement. The objection must be based on reasonable grounds directly related to data protection, privacy, or security. A customer's mere preference against a service provider, or the existence of an alternative provider in the market, is not by itself sufficient grounds for objection unless the agreement or applicable law provides otherwise.

sections.heading: 11. Handling Customer Objections
body: Upon receiving a valid objection, ZynReach may, in its reasonable discretion and consistent with the agreements and applicable law, work with the customer to address the concerns raised; provide additional information about the Sub-processor; apply additional appropriate measures where practicable; propose a suitable alternative if available; re-assess the Sub-processor; or take other appropriate action to reduce risk. ZynReach does not guarantee that every objection will result in removing or replacing a Sub-processor.

sections.heading: 12. If an Objection Cannot Be Resolved
body: Where a customer's objection materially prevents ZynReach from delivering an essential part of the services, and no reasonable resolution is reached within the period specified in the applicable agreement, either party may take the actions set out in the agreement, which may include, depending on the case, terminating the affected part of the services. This Policy must not be interpreted as granting the customer a right of immediate termination or any additional right not expressly set out in the contract or applicable law.

sections.heading: 13. Security & Data Protection
body: ZynReach expects Sub-processors to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect the data processed on its behalf, proportionate to the nature of the service and the level of risk.
list: Access control and least privilege, and multi-factor authentication where appropriate.
Encryption in transit, and encryption at rest where appropriate.
Logging and monitoring, and vulnerability, update, and patch management.
Backup and disaster recovery, and incident management.
Infrastructure protection, personnel and user controls, and access-termination procedures.

sections.heading: 14. Confidentiality
body: ZynReach commits to taking appropriate steps to ensure that Sub-processor personnel authorized to access personal data are bound by appropriate confidentiality obligations, and personal data may not be made available to a Sub-processor's employees or contractors beyond what is necessary to perform the authorized services.

sections.heading: 15. Security Incidents
body: Where a security incident at a Sub-processor affects personal data processed on behalf of ZynReach or its customers, ZynReach seeks to obtain appropriate information from the Sub-processor and take reasonable action to address the incident, including investigating its nature, assessing the scope of impact, taking containment actions, addressing the root cause, applying corrective measures, documenting the actions taken, and providing notifications required by law or contract. An incident at a Sub-processor does not mean that all customer data has been compromised; impact assessment depends on the nature of the incident and the data and systems affected.

sections.heading: 16. Data Subject Requests
body: Where the customer is the Controller and ZynReach is the Processor, ZynReach does not generally handle data-subject requests as Controller of the customer's data; as provided under the DPA, ZynReach may provide reasonable assistance to the customer in handling data-subject requests, and may rely on Sub-processors to carry out certain technical steps necessary for that assistance.

sections.heading: 17. International Data Transfer
body: Data may be processed or made available from locations outside the country where the customer or data subjects are located. Where international data transfer is subject to data-protection laws, ZynReach seeks to apply an appropriate lawful transfer mechanism as applicable, such as an adequacy decision by a competent authority, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), other permitted contractual or regulatory measures, or any other legal mechanism available under applicable law. ZynReach may rely on Sub-processors that in turn use infrastructure or vendors located in multiple countries.

sections.heading: 18. Government Orders & Legal Requests
body: ZynReach or a Sub-processor may be required to disclose data under a court order, a law or regulation, an official request from a competent government authority, or a binding legal obligation. In such cases, ZynReach handles the request per applicable law and, where the law permits, seeks to limit disclosure to what is necessary and to maintain appropriate confidentiality.

sections.heading: 19. Cloud Infrastructure Services
body: ZynReach may use cloud infrastructure and hosting providers to operate the services. These services may rely on multiple components, including compute, storage, database, networking, backup, monitoring, security, content delivery, and disaster recovery, which may result in more than one party being involved in delivering the service's technical infrastructure.

sections.heading: 20. AI Providers
body: Where ZynReach uses third-party artificial intelligence or machine-learning services, the provider may be considered a Sub-processor where personal data is shared with it on the customer's behalf. In such cases, ZynReach seeks to apply appropriate controls covering the scope of data sent, the purpose of processing, use of data for training, retention, access, security, confidentiality, international transfer, and legal requirements. Not all AI service providers can be assumed to have the same data-processing policies; the relevant service is assessed according to its nature and risk.

sections.heading: 21. Payment Services
body: ZynReach may use third-party payment-service providers to process payments and billing. A payment provider may process certain personal or financial data independently as a separate party from ZynReach in some cases. Where the payment provider independently determines the purposes and means of certain processing under applicable law, it may not be considered a Sub-processor for that specific processing.

sections.heading: 22. Support Service Providers
body: ZynReach may use third-party service providers or systems to manage support tickets, customer communications, email, request management, and service-issue handling, with access to data restricted per operational need and applicable controls.

sections.heading: 23. Independent Processing by a Service Provider
body: A third party is not considered a Sub-processor merely because it receives or processes some information relating to the customer. Where a third party independently determines the purposes and means of processing, acts as an independent Controller, or is legally required to process independently, this Policy's Sub-processor provisions may not apply to that processing.

sections.heading: 24. No Sale of Customer Data
body: ZynReach does not grant Sub-processors the right to sell Customer Data or use it for independent advertising or unauthorized commercial purposes, except as may be expressly permitted under the contract or applicable law. Technical processing necessary to deliver, operate, or secure the service is not considered a "sale" of data merely because an external service provider is used.

sections.heading: 25. Use of Data for Analytics Purposes
body: ZynReach or Sub-processors may use certain data for legitimate operational and analytical purposes, such as performance monitoring, error detection, stability improvement, fraud and abuse prevention, security, and capacity planning; such processing must remain within the limits permitted by the agreement and applicable law.

sections.heading: 26. Data Retention & Deletion
body: Upon the end of the need for personal data or the end of the relationship with the customer, data is managed per applicable retention and deletion policies, consistent with the DPA, the contract, and applicable law. Certain copies may persist in backup systems for a limited period due to the nature of backup and disaster-recovery systems, remaining subject to protective controls and not returned to operational use except when necessary.

sections.heading: 27. Monitoring & Re-assessment
body: ZynReach may re-assess Sub-processors from time to time, particularly where the nature of the service or processing risk changes, a security incident occurs, legal requirements change, a material change occurs at the service provider, a new type of data is introduced, or the processing location changes. This does not mean ZynReach is obligated to conduct a full periodic audit of every Sub-processor in all cases.

sections.heading: 28. Audits & Verification
body: ZynReach may use various means to verify the level of security and compliance at its Sub-processors, including security questionnaires, document review, review of certifications and accreditations, independent audit reports, risk assessments, contractual reviews, and available technical evidence. ZynReach may rely on independent reports or certifications rather than conducting a direct audit in every case.

sections.heading: 29. ZynReach's Responsibility
body: Subject to the limitations and exceptions set out in the DPA and applicable commercial agreements, ZynReach remains responsible to the customer for performing its data-processing obligations carried out by Sub-processors to the extent required by law and contract. ZynReach does not bear independent liability for processing carried out by a third party acting as an independent Controller outside the scope of ZynReach's instructions or the relevant contractual relationship.

sections.heading: 30. No Additional Rights Granted
body: This Policy does not grant the customer or any third party any additional rights beyond those set out in the DPA, the master agreement, the Terms of Service, or applicable law, and no provision of this Policy should be interpreted as a guarantee or undertaking that ZynReach will use a specific Sub-processor for the duration of the service, unless a written contract states otherwise.

sections.heading: 31. Amendments to This Policy
body: ZynReach may amend this Policy from time to time to reflect changes in the services or Sub-processors, legal and regulatory developments, technical changes, operational improvements, or security and privacy requirements. The updated version is published through appropriate channels, and where the law or the DPA imposes a specific notice requirement, the notice requirements set out in the relevant document or law are observed.

sections.heading: 32. Relationship with the Data Processing Agreement
body: This Policy is read together with the Data Processing Agreement entered into between ZynReach and the customer. Where there is a discrepancy between this Policy and the DPA regarding the use of Sub-processors, the DPA's provisions govern. In particular, the publication of this Policy must not be interpreted as an implicit amendment of the DPA or a waiver of any contractual right or defense available to ZynReach.

sections.heading: 33. Governing Law & Jurisdiction
body: This Policy is governed by the law applicable to the contractual relationship between ZynReach and the customer, and does not itself create independent jurisdiction unless the relevant contract or a mandatory law provides otherwise.

sections.heading: 34. Contact, Acknowledgment & Legal Notice
body: For inquiries relating to Sub-processors, data protection, or privacy, contact ZynReach through the official communication channels published on the Company's website; correspondence should preferably include the customer's name, entity name, account email, the relevant service name, the Sub-processor's name, and the nature of the objection or request.

By using or continuing to use ZynReach's services, the customer acknowledges that it has reviewed this Policy to the extent permitted by the agreement and applicable law, and that this Policy forms part of ZynReach's privacy and data-processing management framework, without affecting any rights or obligations established under a written agreement or applicable law. This document represents ZynReach's regulatory and contractual framework for managing Sub-processors and does not substitute for specialized legal advice or mandatory requirements that may apply to a particular contractual relationship or jurisdiction. © 2026 Zyntra Digital. All Rights Reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose of This Document
body: This Policy sets out the terms, procedures, and controls governing the request, receipt, review, and use of ZynReach's security and compliance documentation. It aims to balance enabling prospective and current customers to conduct appropriate security and legal due diligence and providing the information needed to assess data-protection and information-security controls, with protecting confidential and sensitive information relating to ZynReach's internal infrastructure, technologies, and processes, preventing unauthorized disclosure or use of documents outside the purpose for which they were provided, and preserving the rights of ZynReach, Zyntra Digital, service providers, partners, and third parties. This Policy is part of ZynReach's governance, security, and compliance framework.

sections.heading: 2. Scope of Application
body: This Policy applies to all requests for documents or information relating to information security, data protection, privacy, compliance, risk management, business continuity, disaster recovery, security-incident management, infrastructure, vendors and sub-processors, customer-data access practices, identity and access controls, audit logs, encryption, backup, security testing, review and assessment processes, the DPA, and enterprise due-diligence documentation.

This Policy covers requests submitted by current and prospective customers, procurement teams, cybersecurity teams, Legal & Compliance teams, data protection officers, customer-appointed auditors, enterprise partners, and legal or security advisors authorized by the customer.

sections.heading: 3. Nature of Security & Compliance Documents
body: ZynReach recognizes that some customers, particularly Enterprise customers, need to conduct a security and legal review before or during contracting. Depending on the nature of the request and the applicable authorization level, ZynReach may provide documents classified into three tiers.
list: Tier 1 — Public Documents: Security Overview, Privacy Policy, Data Processing Agreement, Compliance Overview, Sub-processor Information, Data Residency Information, Security Practices Overview.

Tier 2 — Due-Diligence Documents: Security/Privacy/Compliance Questionnaire, Technical & Organizational Measures (TOMs), and summaries of business continuity, disaster recovery, incident response, access control, encryption, vulnerability management, security testing, data flow, sub-processor details, and data residency.

Tier 3 — Restricted Documents: require legal approval, identity verification of the requesting entity, an NDA, and a legitimate business justification; may include independent audit or assessment reports, security-testing reports, penetration-testing executive summaries, detailed security-architecture information, disaster-recovery test summaries, detailed control evidence, and auditor reports.

sections.heading: 4. Information ZynReach Is Not Obligated to Disclose
body: For security, business, and legal reasons, ZynReach reserves the right to refuse, restrict, or redact any request that includes information that could increase security risk or expose trade secrets, and may provide a redacted version or an executive summary instead of disclosing the original details.
list: Passwords, encryption keys, API keys, access tokens, credentials, and secrets.
Infrastructure keys, firewall-rule details, sensitive internal networks, and sensitive internal endpoints.
Protection mechanisms that could be exploited to bypass controls, and details of unremediated vulnerabilities.
Customer data, personal data not necessary for the assessment, and identifying information about unauthorized personnel.
Undisclosed source code, trade secrets, and information relating to other customers or to service providers subject to contractual restrictions.

sections.heading: 5. Security Documents Are Not Automatically Disclosed
body: Submitting a request form through the website does not create an automatic right to receive all of ZynReach's security, technical, or legal documents, and declining to disclose a particular document is not considered a compliance refusal unless an explicit contractual or legal obligation requires its disclosure.
list: Reviewing the request, verifying the requester's identity and the entity represented, and assessing the purpose of the request.
Determining the appropriate information level, and requesting additional documents, an NDA, or an active contractual agreement.
Declining the request in whole or in part, or providing a redacted version of the document or an alternative summary.

sections.heading: 6. Verifying the Requester's Identity
body: To protect ZynReach and its customers, the Company may request information to verify the requester's identity, such as full name, job title, company name, professional email address, country, purpose of the request, nature of the relationship with ZynReach, and the customer's name or enterprise account where applicable. Requests for restricted documents from anonymous or unprofessional email addresses are not favored without additional verification.

sections.heading: 7. Business/Professional Email
body: For Enterprise requests or requests involving restricted documents, ZynReach may require use of a corporate email address belonging to the requesting entity, and the request may be declined or deferred if it cannot be reasonably verified that the requester represents the entity it claims to represent.

sections.heading: 8. Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
body: ZynReach may require execution of a Non-Disclosure Agreement before disclosing any documents or information classified as Confidential, Restricted, or Highly Confidential; in such cases, disclosure does not become effective until the required approval and signature steps are completed.

sections.heading: 9. Use of Documents
body: When any document or security information is provided, the receiving entity is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use it solely for the purpose of conducting a security, legal, and commercial assessment of ZynReach and its prospective or existing contractual relationship with the recipient.
list: Documents may not be used for marketing or competitive purposes, resold, or published publicly.
They may not be uploaded to public sites, shared with unauthorized parties, or used to evaluate a competitor.
They may not be used in press materials or as an independent reference to prove another party's compliance, except with ZynReach's prior written consent.

sections.heading: 10. Prohibition on Republication
body: Restricted security and compliance documents may not be copied, republished, or distributed, in whole or in part, without ZynReach's prior written consent.
list: Websites, GitHub, and public repositories.
Social media, forums, and public presentations.
Published procurement reports, press reports, and public documents.

sections.heading: 11. Third-Party-Issued Documents
body: ZynReach's documents may include information, reports, certifications, or assessments issued by independent or third-party entities. In such cases, the document is not the exclusive property of ZynReach, its use is subject to any restrictions imposed by its owner, it may not be interpreted beyond its original scope, and ZynReach may not modify the content of a report issued by an independent party in a way that changes its meaning.

sections.heading: 12. Certifications, Frameworks & Standards
body: ZynReach uses terms such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 aligned, GDPR-ready, and CCPA to describe its security and compliance program, and each description must be interpreted according to its actual status, scope, and date.

"Certified" means a valid, formal certification issued by an appropriate accreditation or certification body currently exists. "Audited" means the controls or system have undergone an audit within the scope specified in the report. "Aligned" means the practices or controls are designed or organized to be consistent with a given framework, and does not by itself mean a certification has been obtained. "Ready" means processes or practices are designed to support a given framework's requirements, and does not by itself mean ZynReach has obtained an official certification or accreditation. This distinction is legally important, as ZynReach's current pages use phrasing such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 aligned, and GDPR-ready rather than presenting all of these frameworks as certifications of equal standing.

sections.heading: 13. Documents Do Not Constitute Legal Advice
body: The documents and information ZynReach provides for security and compliance purposes are operational, technical, and business information. They do not constitute legal advice, a legal opinion, a guarantee of the customer's legal compliance, a legal assessment of the customer's operations, or a guarantee that using ZynReach automatically makes the customer compliant with any law. The customer remains responsible for assessing its own compliance with the laws and regulations applicable to its business, sector, and geographic location.

sections.heading: 14. Protection of Personal Data During the Request Process
body: ZynReach commits to processing personal data submitted as part of a security and compliance documentation request per the Privacy Policy and relevant laws. Information provided is used for processing the request, verifying identity, communicating with the requester, managing the due-diligence process, complying with legal obligations, documenting approvals, and managing business relationships. The requester must not send any sensitive personal data or actual customer data that is not explicitly required.

sections.heading: 15. Processing of Customer Data
body: Where ZynReach processes personal data on the customer's behalf, the data-processing relationship may be governed by a separate Data Processing Agreement (DPA), which provides that data is processed per the customer's documented instructions, with provisions relating to sub-processors, security measures, data-subject rights, and international transfers.

sections.heading: 16. Sub-processors
body: ZynReach may use service providers or sub-processors to operate the platform, such as for cloud infrastructure, email delivery, analytics, and customer support; sub-processors and the scope of their use are set out in published or customer-available documentation, consistent with relevant legal and contractual obligations.

sections.heading: 17. International Data Transfer
body: Data may be processed or stored in different geographic locations depending on the infrastructure, plan, and services used. ZynReach's current compliance information indicates that customer data is hosted by default in data centers within the United States, with regional data-residency options available for Enterprise plans where contractually available. Any applicable international data transfer is subject to appropriate legal and contractual controls and safeguards.

sections.heading: 18. Security Incident Management
body: ZynReach maintains a framework for managing and responding to security incidents that includes, as applicable to the incident, detection, severity classification, containment, investigation, remediation, recovery, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and notification of affected parties where legally or contractually required. ZynReach's current security page references a documented incident-response plan, severity and escalation levels, and customer-notification frameworks consistent with applicable regulatory requirements.

sections.heading: 19. Security as an Ongoing Process
body: ZynReach does not guarantee that any information system can be made absolutely immune to all risks or threats. Accordingly, any reference to Secure, Security, Protected, or Enterprise-grade should be understood as describing the security controls and practices applied, not as an absolute guarantee against breach, data loss, service interruption, human error, cyberattack, or security vulnerability. This framing is important to protect the Company from having marketing language interpreted as an absolute guarantee of a security outcome.

sections.heading: 20. Backup & Recovery
body: ZynReach uses backup, restoration, and incident-recovery mechanisms consistent with its adopted operational architecture. However, the existence of backups is not to be interpreted as an absolute guarantee against data loss under all circumstances, and recovery capability depends on the nature and scope of the incident, the data and infrastructure affected, and the recovery procedures in place.

sections.heading: 21. Customer Obligations
body: When using ZynReach, the customer remains responsible for key security and operational matters.
list: Protecting its own login credentials, and not sharing passwords.
Enabling MFA where available, managing user permissions, and removing unauthorized users.
Not uploading unlawful data, and not using the platform to infringe the rights of others.
Complying with laws applicable to its business, determining what data it is entitled to enter into the platform, and applying appropriate data-retention controls.

sections.heading: 22. ZynReach Is Not a Substitute for Customer Security Responsibilities
body: Using ZynReach does not transfer all cybersecurity or data-protection responsibilities to ZynReach. Each party's responsibilities are governed by the service agreement, the DPA where applicable, the Privacy Policy, the Terms of Use, commercial agreements, and applicable laws and regulations. The relationship is viewed as a Shared Responsibility Model depending on the nature of the service and its use.

sections.heading: 23. Obligations of the Customer's Review Team
body: When the customer obtains restricted documents, it must observe strict handling controls.
list: Limiting access to individuals who need it, and protecting the documents from unauthorized access.
Not copying or publishing them beyond the permitted purpose, and not using them to conduct offensive testing against ZynReach.
Not attempting to discover or exploit vulnerabilities based on the information provided.
Notifying ZynReach if the documents are sent to an unauthorized person, and complying with any applicable NDA or confidentiality agreement.

sections.heading: 24. Prohibition on Unauthorized Offensive Testing
body: Providing security or technical documents does not constitute consent to penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, load testing, security testing, automated scanning, reverse engineering, or exploitation attempts. No security testing may be conducted against ZynReach's systems except under prior, explicit written authorization from ZynReach specifying the scope, duration, and systems permitted to be tested.

sections.heading: 25. Document Request Procedure
body: The request process follows a seven-stage sequence.
list: Stage 1 — Submission: name, company, corporate email, job title, type of documents requested, purpose of the request.
Stage 2 — Verification: of the requester's identity, entity, purpose, and required information level.
Stage 3 — Assessment: determining the classification — Public / Confidential / Restricted — based on the nature of the information.
Stage 4 — NDA: where required, the confidentiality agreement is completed.
Stage 5 — Approval: internal approval is obtained per the sensitivity level of the documents.
Stage 6 — Disclosure: documents are sent via the approved method.
Stage 7 — Recording: ZynReach may keep a record of the request and disclosure for governance and audit purposes.

sections.heading: 26. Request Processing Time
body: ZynReach aims to process requests within a reasonable period proportionate to the nature of the request and the level of documents requested; no estimated timeframe constitutes a contractual promise unless expressly agreed in a written agreement. Processing may take longer where legal approval, security review, an NDA, third-party consent, redaction of sensitive information, or additional identity verification of the requester is required.

sections.heading: 27. Document Accuracy & Currency
body: Some security documents or audit reports may relate to a specific time period. A document must always be read together with its issue date, scope, and validity period, if any, and an outdated document may not be used to demonstrate a current security posture without verifying it remains in effect.

sections.heading: 28. Changes to the Security Program
body: ZynReach reserves the right to develop and update its security architecture, controls, service providers, risk-management procedures, incident-response processes, encryption technologies, access policies, backup procedures, and compliance procedures, and some information contained in security documents may change as the platform evolves.

sections.heading: 29. No Additional Guarantees Created
body: No security document, response to a security questionnaire, presentation, or email correspondence creates an additional contractual obligation on ZynReach unless expressly included in a written agreement signed by the parties' authorized representatives. This point is important so that an employee's answer to a Security Questionnaire does not become an independent legal commitment.

sections.heading: 30. Conflicts Between Documents
body: In the event of a conflict between this Policy, Security Documentation, the Privacy Policy, the DPA, the Terms of Service, and the Master Service Agreement, priority of application is determined per the effective contractual agreements between the parties and applicable law. In particular, this Policy is not a substitute for the DPA, the service agreement, or any written commercial agreement.

sections.heading: 31. Intellectual Property Rights
body: All intellectual property rights relating to ZynReach's documents, including content, designs, tables, templates, graphics, security whitepapers, technical documents, and methodologies, remain owned by ZynReach or the relevant rights holders unless a written agreement provides otherwise, and delivering a copy of a document does not transfer its intellectual property to the recipient.

sections.heading: 32. Notification of Leaked or Lost Documents
body: If a recipient becomes aware that a confidential or restricted ZynReach document has been lost, stolen, accessed without authorization, sent to an unauthorized person, or unintentionally published, it must notify ZynReach without undue delay through the official communication channels.

sections.heading: 33. ZynReach's Right to Amend or Withdraw Documents
body: ZynReach reserves the right to update, replace, or withdraw documents, correct errors, reclassify a document, restrict access to it, or issue a new version, and the existence of a prior version does not guarantee its continued validity for use.

sections.heading: 34. No Absolute Security Guarantee
body: While applying appropriate technical and organizational controls, ZynReach acknowledges that information security is affected by the evolving nature of risks, technologies, and threats. Accordingly, ZynReach provides no absolute guarantee that the service will be free of all vulnerabilities, attacks, failures, or security incidents, and any specific contractual warranties are governed exclusively by the signed commercial agreement between the parties.

sections.heading: 35. Governing Law & Jurisdiction
body: This Policy is governed, to the extent permitted by law, by the law applicable to the contractual relationship between ZynReach and the beneficiary entity, and where a master agreement, DPA, or other effective agreement specifies the governing law and jurisdiction, that agreement's provisions govern on this point.

sections.heading: 36. Contacting the Security & Compliance Team & Requester Acknowledgment
body: To request security and compliance documentation or for related inquiries, contact the Security & Compliance Team at security@zynreach.com, the Legal Team for legal inquiries at legal@zynreach.com, and the Privacy Team for privacy and data-protection requests at privacy@zynreach.com.

By submitting a request for security and compliance documentation, the requester acknowledges that the information requested may include confidential or restricted information, and undertakes to use any information provided by ZynReach solely for legitimate security, legal, and business assessment purposes, not to copy, publish, or share it with any unauthorized party, and to comply with any applicable confidentiality agreement or terms of use. The requester further acknowledges that obtaining the documents does not constitute a guarantee or certification of legal compliance in the requesting entity's favor and does not create any additional contractual obligation on ZynReach unless agreed in writing.

sections.heading: 37. Disclaimer
body: The security and compliance information ZynReach provides is intended to help customers and interested parties conduct appropriate due diligence. This information does not constitute an absolute guarantee of security or compliance and does not replace independent legal or security assessment that may be required based on the nature of the customer's business. Any certifications, audits, or compliance frameworks referenced are limited to their scope, period, and issuing body, and may not be interpreted beyond that scope. © 2026 Zyntra Digital.
