sections.heading: 1. Introduction & Parties
body: This Data Processing Agreement ("Agreement" or "DPA") is entered into between Zyntra Digital, as the operator and service provider of the ZynReach platform ("ZynReach" or the "Processor"), and the customer or organization subscribing to ZynReach's services (the "Customer" or the "Controller"). This Agreement governs ZynReach's processing of personal data on the Customer's behalf in connection with the provision of the services.

sections.heading: 2. Purpose & Scope
body: This Agreement sets out the nature, purposes, and duration of personal data processing, the rights and obligations of the parties — including the use of sub-processors, data security, security incident notification, audit rights, data deletion and return, and international transfers.

This Agreement applies whenever ZynReach processes personal data on the Customer's behalf as part of the ZynReach platform and its services (CRM, lead management, business data, marketing automation, sales management, support services, project and document management, AI-enabled features, integrations and APIs, and Enterprise services). This Agreement does not apply to data ZynReach processes as a Controller for its own purposes (such as website administration and direct marketing), which is governed by ZynReach's own Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 3. Definitions
body: For the purposes of this Agreement, the following terms have the meanings set out below:
list: Personal Data: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person under applicable law.
Controller: the party that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data.
Processor: the party that processes personal data on the Controller's behalf.
Data Subject: the natural person to whom personal data relates.
Processing: any operation performed on personal data, including collection, storage, organization, retrieval, use, transmission, alteration, and deletion.
Sub-processor: any third party engaged by ZynReach to process personal data on the Customer's behalf.
Security Incident: any security event affecting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of data or systems.
Personal Data Breach: a security breach leading to, or likely to lead to, the destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or unauthorized access to, personal data.

sections.heading: 4. Relationship to the Master Agreement
body: This Agreement forms part of the commercial agreement entered into between the parties (the Master Services Agreement, or the Terms of Service / Subscription Agreement, as applicable to the Customer). In the event of a direct conflict between this Agreement and the master agreement with respect to the processing of personal data, this Agreement prevails only to the extent necessary to resolve the data protection subject matter.
This Agreement does not modify pricing, service scope, service levels, limitations of liability, intellectual property, or payment terms, unless the master agreement expressly states otherwise.

sections.heading: 5. Roles of the Parties
body: The Customer is the Controller for personal data that it uploads to ZynReach, creates within the platform, collects from its own customers or employees, imports from its own systems, or directs ZynReach to process.
ZynReach acts as a Processor only when it processes Customer data on the Customer's behalf, on the Customer's instructions, and solely for the purpose of providing the services.

sections.heading: 6. Customer Obligations & Warranties
body: The Customer represents and warrants, to the extent permitted by law, that:
list: It has a lawful basis for processing the data and the right to collect it and input it into ZynReach.
It has provided the required notices to data subjects and obtained the necessary consents where required.
It will not use ZynReach in a way that violates the law, and will not upload unnecessary or highly sensitive data without an appropriate lawful basis and safeguards.
It is responsible for the accuracy of the data it provides and for the instructions it issues to ZynReach.

sections.heading: 7. Processing Instructions
body: ZynReach processes personal data in accordance with the master agreement, this DPA, the Customer's documented instructions, and the platform functionality selected by the Customer, and is not responsible for any violation of law by the Customer arising from the nature of the data it entered, the purpose for which it used the data, how it obtained the data, or the instructions it issued.
The following activities constitute approved processing instructions as part of normal use of the platform; additional instructions may be given in writing:
list: Creating accounts, storing data, retrieving it, searching it, and organizing it.
Running reports, exporting data, and executing system operations.
Operating integrations and the features the Customer chooses to use.

sections.heading: 8. Limits on Data Use & Aggregated Data
body: ZynReach may not use Customer data for purposes independent of providing the services, except with the Customer's consent, where legally required, where necessary for security and fraud/abuse prevention, or where the data has been anonymized or aggregated such that it no longer identifies the data subject.

ZynReach may generate aggregated, statistical, or usage-metric data from service-operation data, provided such data does not identify the Customer or any data subject, and use it to improve products, analytics, security, and planning — without this clause granting ZynReach any right to use the Customer's raw personal data for independent purposes.

sections.heading: 9. Categories of Personal Data & Data Subjects
body: Processed data may include the following categories:
list: Identity data (name, username, internal identifier) and contact data (email, phone, address).
Business data (company, job title, department) and customer data (CRM records, leads, contacts, accounts).
Transactional and support data (support messages, help requests, issue records).
Usage data (login events, audit logs, system events) and any personal data contained within a document the Customer uploads.

sections.heading: 10. Special Categories & Children's Data
body: The Customer is not permitted to use ZynReach to process health data, biometric data, sensitive financial data, data concerning sex life, beliefs or origin, or any other special category of data, or children's data as a core part of the service, unless it is necessary for the service, permitted under the agreement, the Customer has an appropriate lawful basis, and the required safeguards have been applied. ZynReach may decline certain types of processing it considers to carry an unacceptable level of risk.

sections.heading: 11. Duration of Processing
body: ZynReach continues to process Customer data for the duration of the Customer's subscription to the services, until the agreement ends, the data is deleted under this DPA, or the Customer's instructions are carried out — subject to applicable legal retention periods, backups, and security records.

sections.heading: 12. Confidentiality & Personnel
body: ZynReach ensures that persons authorized to access the data are bound by confidentiality, are subject to appropriate contractual or statutory obligations, and are granted access on a least-privilege basis; Customer data may not be used outside the scope of the access granted.

ZynReach takes appropriate steps to ensure that employees who can access Customer data are trained, bound by confidentiality, granted the minimum level of privilege necessary, and subject to access-termination procedures once access is no longer needed.

sections.heading: 13. Information Security Measures
body: ZynReach applies technical and organizational measures appropriate to the risk, including but not limited to:
list: Encryption in transit and at rest, access controls and role-based access control, multi-factor authentication, and the principle of least privilege.
Audit logging, security monitoring, and vulnerability management.
Backup, disaster recovery, incident response, and security testing.

These measures evolve over time as risks and technologies develop. The parties acknowledge that no technical environment can be guaranteed to be absolutely secure, and that no reference to encryption, MFA, certifications, or monitoring constitutes a guarantee that a security breach will not occur; ZynReach commits to taking appropriate measures, not to guaranteeing the absence of risk.

sections.heading: 14. Access Control
body: ZynReach applies a "need-to-know / least privilege" principle, and employee or contractor access to Customer data is limited to what is necessary to perform their duties.

sections.heading: 15. Sub-processors
body: The Customer authorizes ZynReach to use sub-processors to provide the service; their categories may include cloud infrastructure, database services, email delivery, customer support, monitoring, analytics, security, AI infrastructure, and payment services. ZynReach remains contractually responsible for its sub-processors' obligations to the extent provided under law and this Agreement.

ZynReach may add or replace sub-processors as operationally or technically necessary, and seeks to provide appropriate information about them through the mechanism maintained on its trust center. Where the law or this Agreement grants the Customer a right to object to a new sub-processor, the objection must be in writing, based on data-protection grounds, and submitted within the specified period; it may not be used as a means of disrupting the service without legitimate cause.

sections.heading: 16. Data Subject Requests
body: When the Customer receives a request from a data subject relating to their data held within ZynReach, the Customer handles it as the Controller. ZynReach assists the Customer, to a reasonable and appropriate extent and within the platform's capabilities, with access, correction, deletion, restriction, export, and search.

If ZynReach receives a request directly from a data subject regarding Customer data, it will, where permitted by law, refer the request to the Customer rather than responding to it independently on the Customer's behalf, unless the law requires ZynReach to respond directly.

sections.heading: 17. Regulatory Cooperation & DPIA Support
body: ZynReach provides, within reasonable limits, the assistance necessary for the Customer to meet its obligations relating to processing security, data subject requests, data breach incidents, Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), and regulatory requests; additional assistance requiring substantial resources is subject to agreed fees unless prohibited by law.
ZynReach does not provide legal or regulatory advice, and the Customer remains responsible for determining which legal requirements apply to its own activities.

sections.heading: 18. Personal Data Breach Notification
body: Upon becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer data, ZynReach will, in accordance with applicable law and this Agreement, notify the Customer without undue delay. The notification will include, to the extent available, the nature of the incident, the date of discovery, the data affected, the measures taken, remedial actions, and contact details for the response team.

Not every failed login attempt, malware alert, vulnerability, or service interruption necessarily constitutes a personal data breach; ZynReach determines whether an event constitutes an actual breach based on the facts, the risk involved, and applicable law. Upon an incident affecting its account, the Customer must cooperate with ZynReach, provide necessary information, and not obstruct response efforts.

sections.heading: 19. Government & Third-Party Requests
body: If ZynReach receives a lawful request for Customer data, it may disclose it to the extent required by law, and, where permitted, seeks to notify the Customer, define the scope of the request, and limit the data disclosed — without guaranteeing that notice can be given in every case where the law prohibits it.
Where permitted by law, ZynReach may publish or update general information about government requests and legal proceedings.

sections.heading: 20. International Data Transfers
body: Data may be processed outside the country of the Customer or the data subjects; where data is subject to a data-protection regime such as the GDPR or an equivalent, ZynReach uses an appropriate lawful transfer mechanism, which may include an adequacy decision, the European Union's Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), or other appropriate safeguards.

Where necessary, ZynReach reasonably cooperates with the Customer on international transfer risk assessments, while the Customer remains responsible for assessing whether a given transfer meets its own legal requirements. Data storage and processing locations are set out in Annex B, and may change for operational or security reasons, subject to legal and contractual requirements.

sections.heading: 21. Audit Rights
body: The Customer may request reasonable information to demonstrate ZynReach's compliance with its data-protection obligations, such as security documentation, certifications, audit reports, policies, penetration-test summaries, and sub-processor information — subject to confidentiality, security, and intellectual-property protection. No audit may disrupt the service, endanger ZynReach's systems, or disclose another customer's data, trade secrets, encryption keys, or credentials.

ZynReach may satisfy audit requirements by providing SOC reports, ISO certificates, and independent audit reports in lieu of allowing direct technical audits, where sufficient under law. Where an on-site audit is legally required and cannot be satisfied by alternative means, its timing, scope, and duration are agreed in advance with due regard for security and confidentiality, and the Customer bears its reasonable costs unless the law or the agreement provides otherwise.

sections.heading: 22. Record Retention
body: ZynReach may retain processing, security, or audit records for as long as necessary for compliance, security, fraud prevention, dispute resolution, and the defense of legal rights.

sections.heading: 23. Data Return & Deletion
body: Upon termination of the service, the Customer may request an export of its data within the platform's capabilities; the export format, timeframe, and scope are determined by the service and the agreement.

After the agreement ends, ZynReach deletes or renders Customer data unidentifiable according to its standard deletion cycle, unless the Customer requests retention, the law requires it, or the data resides in backups subject to an independent retention cycle. Some data may persist in backups, disaster-recovery systems, and archives after deletion from production systems, and is removed according to the applicable technical retention cycle.

The Customer may request early deletion of data before the contractual retention period ends; the response to such a request may be subject to legal or contractual constraints or additional fees where extensive manual processing is required.

sections.heading: 24. Data & Intellectual Property Ownership
body: Data uploaded by the Customer to ZynReach remains owned by the Customer or the party legally entitled to it; this Agreement does not transfer ownership of that data to ZynReach.

In turn, this Agreement grants the Customer no rights in ZynReach's source code, architecture, algorithms, software, databases, security systems, trade secrets, or documentation, which remain owned by their respective owners. ZynReach may use system metrics, aggregated statistics, de-identified information, and platform telemetry in accordance with this Agreement, the master agreement, and the Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 25. Artificial Intelligence Processing
body: When the Customer uses AI features, the data necessary to operate the feature is processed; the Customer must use it in accordance with the documentation, must not input data it lacks the right to use, must not use AI to make unlawful decisions, and must apply human oversight where appropriate.

Certain AI features may rely on third-party AI infrastructure or service providers, disclosed as part of the sub-processor framework and subject to this Agreement's sub-processor provisions. Unless expressly agreed otherwise, this Agreement does not grant ZynReach a general license to use Customer content to train general-purpose AI models independent of the service; data may be used to operate the requested features and for security and service improvement, in accordance with the agreement and applicable law.

sections.heading: 26. Third-Party Integrations & APIs
body: When the Customer connects ZynReach to a third-party service, the Customer is responsible for choosing that service and consents to sharing the data required for the integration; the third party is governed by its own terms and privacy policy, and ZynReach is not responsible for that party's processing once data has passed to it outside ZynReach's control.

When using APIs, the Customer is responsible for protecting access keys, managing permissions, monitoring usage, and preventing key-sharing; ZynReach may suspend an access key where its use is found to pose a security risk.

sections.heading: 27. Customer Security Obligations
body: The Customer must use multi-factor authentication where available, protect accounts and not share passwords, manage users and review their permissions, remove inactive users, and secure devices used to sign in; ZynReach is not responsible for any breach resulting directly from the Customer's negligence in protecting its own login credentials.

Users to whom the Customer grants access to ZynReach are considered users authorized by the Customer, and the Customer is responsible for their actions, their permissions, the data they enter, and their use of the platform.

sections.heading: 28. Liability & Force Majeure
body: Each party is liable for damages resulting from its material breach of its obligations under law and the commercial agreement; this Agreement does not create an independent indemnification regime that exceeds the liability limits set out in the master agreement, unless mandatory law provides otherwise. Merely describing data as personal, confidential, or sensitive does not override the agreed liability cap.

ZynReach is not responsible for delay or failure to perform resulting from events beyond its reasonable control, such as natural disasters, wars, large-scale attacks, or infrastructure outages, while taking reasonable steps to mitigate the impact of such events.

sections.heading: 29. Term & Termination
body: This Agreement takes effect when signed by the parties, accepted by the Customer as part of a subscription, or when use of the service begins, and continues for as long as ZynReach processes Customer data. It ends upon termination of the master agreement or subscription, or when all processing activities cease.
Provisions that by their nature survive termination remain in effect, including confidentiality, data deletion, records, liability, audit, and legal obligations.

sections.heading: 30. General Provisions
body: The Customer may not assign this Agreement or its rights under it without regard to the terms of the master agreement; ZynReach may transfer this Agreement to an affiliate or legal successor in the event of restructuring, merger, acquisition, or sale of business, with data protection continuing under applicable law.

If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain unaffected, and the unenforceable provision is replaced with one that most closely achieves its intended commercial and legal purpose. ZynReach may update this Agreement where necessary due to legal, regulatory, or technical change, notifying the Customer where required; this Agreement is governed by the law specified in the master commercial agreement.

Privacy-related notices should be sent to privacy@zynreach.com, legal notices to legal@zynreach.com, and security notices to security@zynreach.com. The parties may execute this Agreement electronically, and electronic signatures are valid and effective to the extent permitted by applicable law.

sections.heading: 31. Annexes
body: This Agreement includes a number of detailed annexes that form an integral part of it:
list: Annex A: Processing details (subject matter, duration, nature, and purposes).
Annexes B and C: Categories of personal data and categories of data subjects.
Annex D: Detailed security measures (access control, encryption, monitoring, infrastructure, resilience, incident response, personnel).
Annex E: Sub-processor framework and categories.
Annex F: Data breach response procedure.
Annex G: Data subject request procedure.
Annex H: Data return and deletion procedure.
Annex I: International data transfer procedure.
Annex J: Additional provisions on AI processing.
Annex K: Security and compliance documentation available to Enterprise customers.
Annex L: Order of precedence among documents in the event of conflict.
Enterprise customers may request the full, countersigned copy of this Agreement, including all annexes, by contacting legal@zynreach.com.
